name: Andrew Sypher, Turning Point USA
subject: We don't have enough of these right now
body:
We have more students stepping up than we can fully support at the moment.

| | | [](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z0fdvkmbhqg7d1jham40c1rccgjbbnm97khq48vg_rp22sh2s8i6epr0sdg6ep76cph2bs)
---
| | Friend,
---
I want to give you a picture of what's really happening right now -- not the polished version, but what it actually looks like on the ground.

Inside our office, tables are covered in supplies and open boxes. Coworkers are coming together, packing materials, sealing kits, and sending them out the door as fast as possible.
---
[](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z1khhet34qlstteevg7585deo8efuf2h933ik4s0_rp22sh2s8i6epr0sdg6ep76cph2bs)
---
_Above: Activism kits bound for new chapters being packed with Constitutions, chapter handbooks, American flags, and more at TPUSA HQ in Arizona_
---
These boxes aren't sitting around waiting for someone to need them.

They're already claimed. And we don't have extras.

By the time one batch goes out, more requests come in.

Different schools, different students, same situation -- they want to start something, and they're asking us to help them do it.

That's where things stand right now.

We have more students stepping up than we can fully support at the moment.

And I don't say that lightly.

Because for years, the challenge wasn't getting students the tools -- it was getting them to speak up at all. Most kept their heads down.

The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great.

And for a long time, it worked. But that's all changing.

Now, we're seeing students stand up and push back.

**We saw it clearly at Wheeling High School in the Chicago suburbs -- Charlie's alma mater. **

For the first time, students there launched a Club America chapter. It took months to get approved, but a chapter is finally there.

And now, students are standing outside with signs about free markets and freedom -- not because it's easy, but because they've decided it matters more than staying quiet.
---
[](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zlpa083akivbngm1iljas1n6ktn1uie8u7nvdito_rp22sh2s8i6epr0sdg6ep76cph2bs)
---
That's not something you can just manufacture. But it is something you can support when it happens.

And it's not isolated growth anymore.

**We 're now working with more than 1,450 college chapters and over 3,400 high school chapters across the country. That's real scale. **

But if you zoom out, there are roughly 27,000 high schools in America.

That means tens of thousands of campuses where the Left still dominates the conversation...

And where students are waiting for someone to help them stand up and speak.

So as much as this has grown, we're still in the early innings of what Charlie actually set out to build.

What's different now is the pace.

**Many states are moving to bring Club America chapters to every high school statewide, including: **

✅ Arkansas
✅ Florida
✅ Idaho
✅ Indiana
✅ Montana
✅ Nebraska
✅ Oklahoma
✅ South Carolina
✅ Texas
✅ Tennessee

That brings us to ten states now taking this seriously -- not just talk, but action.
---
[](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zj08rno2mfik8mnufl5kna8g6rbccjpvutc7nsc0_rp22sh2s8i6epr0sdg6ep76cph2bs)
---
That kind of expansion doesn't happen slowly.

It stacks quickly -- and it creates pressure behind the scenes to keep up.

Because every new chapter, every new student leader, every new school means more materials, more support, more follow-through.

And right now, that's where we're stretched.

We're not lacking interest or momentum.

We're working to keep up with both.

_So here 's how you can help... _

Right now, there are students ready to step up -- they just need the tools to do it.

**An activism kit puts everything they need directly into their hands: **

✅ Constitutions.
✅ Chapter guides.
✅ Flags.
✅ Materials to organize and lead.

It turns a student who wants to speak up... _into one who actually does. _

And you'll make it possible for us to keep saying yes when a student reaches out and says, "I want to start something here."

**[Each activism kit costs $25 to pack and ship to a student chapter. Will you put one into a student's hands today?](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zanpqafr94hfpevsvvl0q14avsrj3nr6dbd62gs0_rp22sh2s8i6epr0sdg6ep76cph2bs)**
---
[ **Sponsor an Activism Kit**
**Make Your Gift Here**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zd0gqtpn03r6glj3ss0egg54e4ljhrv2q88mcumo_rp22sh2s8i6epr0sdg6ep76cph2bs)
---
Every activism kit you help sponsor means one more student is ready to lead instead of sitting on the sidelines.

That's how we keep saying "yes" when the next student steps forward.

That's how this movement actually scales.

Because the reality is, the demand is here now.

The only question is whether we're equipped to meet it.

And that comes down to whether people like you decide to step in and help carry this forward.

**[Please commit to sending an activism kit to a conservative student today-- and help us keep building a generation that's willing to stand up and fight for this country.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zjeu24irbi6fmi1k54d64d6v5ok1h5foibsqjv60_rp22sh2s8i6epr0sdg6ep76cph2bs)**
---
[ **Sponsor an Activism Kit**
**Make Your Gift Here**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zndes9c7vruc6u0g2fl42s3jg963lmp9v0qqs5tg_rp22sh2s8i6epr0sdg6ep76cph2bs)
---
One final thing: I also wanted to say thank you.

If you've supported Turning Point USA before -- whether once or many times -- you've already played a role in building what you're seeing right now.

Students finding their voice. More state partnerships. New TPUSA chapters like the one at Charlie's former high school.

This kind of momentum doesn't happen without people willing to stand behind it.

And we don't take that lightly.

I appreciate you taking the time to read this, and for everything you've already done to support this work.
---
| | **For Charlie,** **Andrew Sypher** Chief Field OfficerTurning Point USA
---
[](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z1jnk89ktouqau40fnkum2qaseido4et8rtljf6g_rp22sh2s8i6epr0sdg6ep76cph2bs)
---
[ _**Support Turning Point USA**_](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z7k10eluafvisl7l1li2js7ao20l6dk25cbnmlq8_rp22sh2s8i6epr0sdg6ep76cph2bs)
---
**P.S.** Friend, what you're seeing right now is something we've been working toward for years -- a generation of young Americans who are no longer willing to sit quietly while the Left dominates their schools and culture.

But moments like this don't sustain themselves.

If we don't keep up, we lose ground. It's that simple.

**We need to keep pace with the growth happening right now -- to fund more activism kits, support more chapters, and make sure no student is left standing alone after they decide to speak up. **

If you've already supported Turning Point USA in the past, thank you for carrying this movement forward every single day.

If you haven't yet, I'm asking you to step in now.

**[Help sponsor more activism kits today-- and help us keep building the next generation of Americans who are proud of their country and willing to fight for it.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zb709k4p12upu5ibkvgk11l72hrc92tmqhlko900_rp22sh2s8i6epr0sdg6ep76cph2bs)**
---

Phoenix, Arizona 85044

# Conforti Grassroots Newsletter
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |

Welcome to the inaugural edition of our interactive grassroots newsletter. As we approach the Midterm Election 2026, this newsletter is dedicated to keeping the hardworking constituents of Illinois' 6th Congressional District informed and engaged.

Our campaign is built on a "district-first" mentality. We are committed to prioritizing your needs, focusing on fundamental ideals of sensible solutions and open dialogue. Through this newsletter, we will provide you with regular updates on policy, campaign events, and current community events happening right here in our district.
Click the button below to make a donation today. Your donations are what makes this possible.
---
| | [DONATE](https://conforti4congress.us6.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7fd34b7284bf7f5e87a4e45e5&id=9938759a86&e=25f4fa3311)
---
| |
---
| |
## Kitchen Table Tuesday.
The Conforti Brief.
District-First Events.
---
| |
### Educate. Inform. Invite.
---
| |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
# Kitchen Table Tuesday
---
| | **Educating and connecting** with voters on important issues.
---
| | |
---
| | The current healthcare system has led to **unaffordable plans and confusion** for most Americans and small businesses. Ironically, politicians call it the Affordable Care Act, but it has been unaffordable for most Americans and small businesses. Many counties only have two options for consumers, and our healthcare costs have only gone up over the last decade. Having worked in the healthcare industry, Niki Conforti knows we can and must do better for the hardworking people of Illinois.
To address this critical issue, the campaign's goal is to push for real reform that increases transparency in medical billing, to foster competition among healthcare systems. The impact of this approach - by driving up competition in the marketplace - costs are lowered for patients and families gain more flexibility in their coverage options. By giving families more choices and requiring transparent pricing, these initiatives will ultimately make healthcare more accessible and more affordable across our district.
---
| |
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | |
## The Conforti Brief
---
| | **Informing voters** on current events and how Niki plans to help them once in office.
---
| | Recently, the Wall Street Journal reported an alarming economic milestone: the U.S. national debt has officially topped 100% of our Gross Domestic Product (GDP), for the first time since 1946. This unchecked borrowing is causing our country to approach nearly $40 Trillion in national debt. We are placing an enormous and unsustainable burden on our children and grandchildren.
.Washington's runaway debt is a direct result of the **Left's radical spending agenda**. Democrats, like my opponent Sean Casten, are pushing for increased spending on nonessential programs that benefit people in foreign countries, while forgetting about hardworking American families.
According to the National Taxpayers Union, Sean Casten has earned the **“Big Spender”** designation, for failures in reigning in wasteful spending in DC. More spending inevitably leads to more taxes. Illinoisans are already regularly burdened with higher tolls and higher taxes, and I oppose any further tax and fee hikes on our residents.
I am running for Congress because we need to curb this reckless spending and stop tax increases on working families. When elected to represent the 6th District, I will take direct action to address this crisis by:

1. Implementing Spending Caps: I will work to push for spending caps to limit the amount we add to the national debt in order to pay for the Left's radical spending;

2. Holding the Line on the Debt Ceiling: By the time the next Congress takes office, the issue of the Debt Ceiling will be back on the table. I am opposed to raising the Debt Ceiling, and I will push to curb spending and limit the debt we incur as a Nation;

3. Investigating Fraud and Abuse: The oversight committee must investigate the extensive fraud and abuse of taxpayer dollars that is currently draining our treasury.
.

We** can’t **tax and spend our way to prosperity. It is time for sensible solutions that protect your wallet and secure our nation's financial future.

Stay informed on this issue—[**read the full breakdown here**](https://conforti4congress.us6.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7fd34b7284bf7f5e87a4e45e5&id=82e17b4b4b&e=25f4fa3311)**.**

---
| |
---

# District-First
# Events
---
| | **Inviting voters** to community events and how they can get involved!**
**Join the Conforti Campaign at the**108th Elmhurst Memorial Day Parade**!
---
| |
---
| | We warmly invite you to participate and walk alongside Niki Conforti and our campaign team at the 108th Elmhurst Memorial Day Parade! Come out to show your support for our "District-First" vision and join the community for this historic occasion. This year's parade blends time-honored remembrance with a spirit of national celebration, honoring the sacrifices of our brave men and women in uniform while recognizing the **250th birthday of the United States**!

1. Date: **Monday, May 25, 2026**

2. Time: The parade steps off at **9:30 AM (CDT)**

3. Location: The route begins at the **Elmhurst City Centre at Third and York** , and will proceed to the Elmhurst Veterans Memorial in Wilder Park.

Post-Parade: A solemn Memorial Day Ceremony will be held immediately following the parade at Wilder Park to continue the tradition of respectful remembrance.
Bring your family, friends, and neighbors to walk with us as we share Niki's platform of sensible solutions, economic affordability, and community safety with the voters of DuPage County.
We would love to have you join our ranks for this special day!
To get more details, or reserve your **free campaign t-shirt** , please contact our team at [_info@conforti4congress.com_](mailto:info@conforti4congress.com?subject=Event%20Information&body=) _._

We look forward to celebrating with you!

# How Faith Shapes Culture & Politics
---
| |
---
| | What happens when faith collides with politics and culture? In our latest podcast episode, Lance Wallnau — the minister behind the Seven Mountains of Culture framework — breaks down why the church can no longer sit on the sidelines and what everyday believers can actually do about it. Wallnau challenges believers to step out of the pews and into the arenas of media, education, government, and beyond, making a compelling case that faith was never meant to stay inside the four walls of a church. If you've ever felt the tension between your beliefs and the world around you, this episode will ignite that fire, giving you clarity, courage, and a practical path forward. Listen to the full episode on your preferred podcast platform and share it with every mom who needs to hear it: [YouTube](https://momsforamerica.us/so/ddPuJulF-/c?w=uoYF8gjEFssXpt5eRl6gal21rJByM_zhjYxKbu1wMSQ.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vQE1vbXNmb3JBbWVyaWNhIiwiciI6Ijc4N2IzNTI1LTIzYzYtNDc3NS1iMGYyLTAxNDFjYzAyNDc1ZiIsIm0iOiJtYWlsIiwiYyI6IjRhYTNmYzQzLWRiNWUtNDE2Ni05YmMyLWQ3ZGZiNzJkNzIxNCJ9), [Rumble](https://momsforamerica.us/so/ddPuJulF-/c?w=uJxSBb-xW67XBIlYtGSA6xVpnUyj9KOA-XaUxvogsFQ.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ydW1ibGUuY29tL2MvYy0xMjA2NzMzP2U5cz1zcmNfdjFfY2JsIiwiciI6Ijc4N2IzNTI1LTIzYzYtNDc3NS1iMGYyLTAxNDFjYzAyNDc1ZiIsIm0iOiJtYWlsIiwiYyI6IjRhYTNmYzQzLWRiNWUtNDE2Ni05YmMyLWQ3ZGZiNzJkNzIxNCJ9), [Spotify](https://momsforamerica.us/so/ddPuJulF-/c?w=gS7F9k4pdVGi7qwg7aD6LxmzBuGeSmcI-uwYBgNe2_A.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9vcGVuLnNwb3RpZnkuY29tL3Nob3cvMHBIemFBWGJCRVVFUlBxajluQlhxYyIsInIiOiI3ODdiMzUyNS0yM2M2LTQ3NzUtYjBmMi0wMTQxY2MwMjQ3NWYiLCJtIjoibWFpbCIsImMiOiI0YWEzZmM0My1kYjVlLTQxNjYtOWJjMi1kN2RmYjcyZDcyMTQifQ) or [Apple](https://momsforamerica.us/so/ddPuJulF-/c?w=EhKd_SCUQUgF68faQpr-ojmLV0IE91NIvhCTpWmj9gY.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9wb2RjYXN0cy5hcHBsZS5jb20vdXMvcG9kY2FzdC9tb21zLWZvci1hbWVyaWNhLXBvZGNhc3QvaWQxNjE2OTIwMTIxIiwiciI6Ijc4N2IzNTI1LTIzYzYtNDc3NS1iMGYyLTAxNDFjYzAyNDc1ZiIsIm0iOiJtYWlsIiwiYyI6IjRhYTNmYzQzLWRiNWUtNDE2Ni05YmMyLWQ3ZGZiNzJkNzIxNCJ9).

### The 7 Mountains of Influence in America and Why They Matter
---
| |
---
| | There is danger for families around almost every corner — from social media and streaming entertainment to concerning ideologies in many American classrooms. As conservatives, we hold that faith, traditional values, family, and patriotism are key to a prosperous America. But arguing doesn't seem to be doing the trick. So what's left? In 1975, Christian leaders Loren Cunningham and Bill Bright independently discovered the same revelation — that seven mountains of influence shape every nation: Family, Religion, Education, Media, Entertainment, Business, and Government. Whoever occupies these mountains shapes the culture. You don't have to run for office or produce a Hollywood film to make a difference. Every mom raising children with strong values, choosing faith-based education, and voting her convictions is already influencing these mountains. Read the full blog and take the next step by joining our free membership at Moms TownSquare.

In our latest podcast episode, Lance Wallnau — the minister behind the Seven Mountains of Culture framework — breaks down why the church can no longer sit on the sidelines and what everyday believers can actually do about it. Wallnau challenges believers to step out of the pews and into the arenas of media, education, government, and beyond, making a compelling case that faith was never meant to stay inside the four walls of a church. If you have read the first two pieces in this series, you know I want Mississippi to win the data-center boom. I think we should welcome it and stop apologizing for wanting investment in our state. That is the conservative case for data centers.
This piece is the conservative case against the way Mississippi is paying for them.
Let me say plainly what our state has done. In a January 2024 special session, the Legislature approved a massive incentive package for Amazon Web Services in Madison County. The package included $44 million in direct taxpayer cash, including workforce-training subsidies that shifted costs from Amazon onto taxpayers, along with a $215 million state loan for roads, water, sewer infrastructure, and a fire station. The deal also included a renewable 30-year tax exemption triggered by continued investment of at least $500 million annually, a 3.15% rebate on construction costs, full exemption from sales and use tax on equipment, and free rights to install company fiber in public utility right-of-way. The headline value of the package, not counting the standing tax exemptions, was roughly $260 million.
These are subsidies. Big, public, generational subsidies. They are not capitalism.
Then in April 2026, Amazon expanded its Mississippi commitment to $25 billion across additional sites, all of them eligible for the same standing exemptions.
Mississippi's standing data-center incentive program, on the books since 2019, exempts certified data-center companies from state sales and use tax, corporate income tax, and franchise tax for ten years. xAI's $20 billion Southaven campus falls under that program. Compass Datacenters' $10 billion Meridian project qualifies not only for those exemptions, but also for a $4 million state site grant and eligibility for the Advantage Jobs program, which can return up to 90% of employee state income-tax withholding back to the company for ten years.
The Center for Economic Accountability, an independent watchdog group focused on subsidy policy, named the Compass deal the worst economic-development deal in the United States for 2025.
The argument we are constantly given is that the state will eventually earn this money back through economic growth. I would like to believe that. But independent audits do not back it up.
When Georgia's own state auditor analyzed what else the state could have done with the forgone tax revenue from data-center incentives, the return collapsed from the headline claim of $11 in economic activity for every $1 of lost revenue down to about $1.33 for every $1 foregone. In other words, the incentives barely broke even, and only under the assumption that Georgia could not have used the same money more effectively elsewhere, whether on roads, schools, or returning it directly to taxpayers.
A separate independent assessment found Georgia's tax exemptions were actually decisive for only about 30% of the data centers built there. The state had previously assumed the figure was 90%. In other words, many of those projects likely would have happened even without the subsidies.
Good Jobs First, one of the leading watchdog organizations tracking state subsidy programs, estimates the average data-center megadeal in America now costs taxpayers roughly $1.9 million per permanent job created. In Nevada, the only state that publicly reports actual permanent-worker wages for these projects, the average salary is about $65,000 a year, well below the figures commonly used in splashy press announcements. Of the 32 states offering data-center incentives, 12 do not even publish aggregate revenue losses, and not one publishes actual permanent jobs created versus jobs promised.
Here is the test.
xAI built its first Memphis supercomputer campus without taking a single PILOT or EDGE incentive from the State of Tennessee. Memphis is still collecting full property taxes on the project, estimated at roughly $13 million to $20 million annually, and reinvesting a portion of that revenue directly into surrounding neighborhoods through a community-benefit ordinance.
Same company. Same technology. Same kind of project. No subsidy.
That should at least force Mississippi taxpayers to ask whether these subsidies are actually necessary on our side of the state line.
A real conservative position on this is not anti-investment. It is anti-corporate welfare.
The state should make it easy to do business in Mississippi. Streamline permitting. Pre-approve industrial sites. Build infrastructure that benefits every industrial user instead of a single politically connected company. Enforce environmental standards fairly and predictably. Charge market rates for water and electricity.
That is what governments are for.
What governments are not for is writing checks to trillion-dollar corporations because we have convinced ourselves they will only come if we pay them to.
If a data-center project only works because taxpayers absorb the cost and the risk, it is not real economic development. It is a transfer from working Mississippians to shareholders in California and Seattle, dressed up in a press release.
I want the data centers. I do not want my neighbors to pay for them.
Those two sentences are the same sentence, and it is the one our governor, our Legislature, and our Public Service Commission ought to hear from every conservative in this state, loudly and often.
In the next piece in this series, I want to make the argument I find hardest to walk away from: Mississippi has been through this cycle before. The historical record is sitting right in front of us. We just keep choosing not to read it.

### Independent power producers are sitting on capital and profits while Pennsylvania families pay the price. It's time to change that.
| | [Patrick J. Murphy](https://substack.com/@patrickmurphypa)
---
| May 12
---

Across America, including in my home state of Pennsylvania, electricity costs continue to rise, hitting family budgets, small businesses, and the price of nearly everything we buy. My neighbors are feeling it here in Bucks County. Governor Josh Shapiro is right that Pennsylvania's electric grid is under real strain. His[ recent budget address and letter to utility companies](https://substack.com/redirect/1d7a6536-f05c-4478-bf8c-9e6c804a0651?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) show he's paying attention.
Now comes the harder part: identifying the actual cause.
It's easy to blame utilities for higher electricity rates, but that misses the real problem. Focusing on blame distracts us from the main issue we need to solve if we want lower costs and better reliability.
In Pennsylvania today, utilities are largely blocked from owning power plants and competing in the market to generate power. Instead, the Commonwealth relies on PJM Interconnection, a regional grid operator that governs electricity markets across multiple states. Under that system, independent power producers generate electricity and sell it into wholesale auctions, and utilities are required to purchase that power on behalf of their customers.
Utilities then deliver that electricity to homes and businesses through Pennsylvania. They make a return only on the cost of transmitting that power to your home.

When supply is tight, prices rise. Because electricity in PJM is priced through auctions, consumers pay the highest clearing price. The ceiling on these auctions is growing, so power bills keep rising without a plan to address it. Moreover, independent producers are making massive profits from those auctions where the price just keeps rising because they are the only suppliers in the state. Everyone in the electricity business obviously makes money, yes, but utility companies are regulated by the state Public Utility Commission that controls their charges. Governor Shapiro is rightfully examining that, according to his letter, but should also look into these independent producers and their culpability with high prices. It's about supply and demand.
Electricity demand is growing in Pennsylvania and throughout PJM's multi-state footprint. At the same time, older power plants are retiring, and new resources have not been built fast enough to replace them. Independent power producers, many of them large corporations, own the power plants but have largely failed to develop any new projects. They have access to [capital and profits](https://substack.com/redirect/4715ed6b-e26d-4da8-9cff-da6621123c17?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), but have failed to propose enough quick options to increase power generation to make more supply available for consumers.
That is the real problem--not utility rates, delivery costs, line workers, or local infrastructure. It comes down to supply.
As someone who served in Congress on the Energy and Water subcommittee on Appropriations, I've always advocated for an 'all-of-the-above energy policy.' The federal government has cut incentives for clean energy, making Governor Shapiro's focus on supply even more important. He is right to highlight rising electricity prices. Now we need to look at the cause. To lower prices, we need to add more power to the grid. That means rethinking the rules that limit who can build new generation.
If independent power producers can build new plants, utilities should be able to as well. Let them compete, invest, create jobs, and help meet the growing demand for electricity.
Pennsylvania residents cannot prosper if we keep using a system that limits supply and raises costs. The issue is complicated, but the solution does not have to be.
We need more power generation, more competition, and must solve a supply problem through true action, together. Governor Shapiro started the conversation by taking action. Now it is time for all affected parties and officials to come together to finish it. Pennsylvania's future depends on making the right choices.
_Honorable Patrick J. Murphy was the 32nd Army Under Secretary and the first Iraq Veteran in Congress. He leads the Geopolitical Unit at Hilco Global._

Instead, the Commonwealth relies on PJM Interconnection, a regional grid operator that governs electricity markets across multiple states. Under that system, independent power producers generate electricity and sell it into wholesale auctions, and utilities are required to purchase that power on behalf of their customers. Utilities then deliver that electricity to homes and businesses through Pennsylvania. They make a return only on the cost of transmitting that power to your home. The Secretary's SitRep is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. When supply is tight, prices rise. Because electricity in PJM is priced through auctions, consumers pay the highest clearing price. The ceiling on these auctions is growing, so power bills keep rising without a plan to address it. Moreover, independent producers are making massive profits from those auctions where the price just keeps rising because they are the only suppliers in the state. Everyone in the electricity business obviously makes money, yes, but utility companies are regulated by the state Public Utility Commission that controls their charges. Governor Shapiro is rightfully examining that, according to his letter, but should also look into these independent producers and their culpability with high prices. It's about supply and demand. Electricity demand is growing in Pennsylvania and throughout PJM's multi-state footprint. At the same time, older power plants are retiring, and new resources have not been built fast enough to replace them. Independent power producers, many of them large corporations, own the power plants but have largely failed to develop any new projects. They have access to , but have failed to propose enough quick options to increase power generation to make more supply available for consumers. That is the real problem--not utility rates, delivery costs, line workers, or local infrastructure. It comes down to supply. As someone who served in Congress on the Energy and Water subcommittee on Appropriations, I've always advocated for an 'all-of-the-above energy policy.' The federal government has cut incentives for clean energy, making Governor Shapiro's focus on supply even more important. He is right to highlight rising electricity prices. Now we need to look at the cause. To lower prices, we need to add more power to the grid. That means rethinking the rules that limit who can build new generation. If independent power producers can build new plants, utilities should be able to as well. Let them compete, invest, create jobs, and help meet the growing demand for electricity. Pennsylvania residents cannot prosper if we keep using a system that limits supply and raises costs. The issue is complicated, but the solution does not have to be. We need more power generation, more competition, and must solve a supply problem through true action, together. Governor Shapiro started the conversation by taking action. Now it is time for all affected parties and officials to come together to finish it. Pennsylvania's future depends on making the right choices. Honorable Patrick J. Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime.

Hello,
**My name is Eileen Laubacher, and I am the Democrat and retired U.S. Navy Rear Admiral running against Lauren Boebert here in Colorado.**
I was 17-years-old the first time I raised my right hand and took an oath to support and defend the Constitution against all enemies, foreign and domestic.
I took those words, and that responsibility, seriously every day for the next 4 decades. When I was an intelligence officer. When I was deployed to Afghanistan. When I became an Admiral. And as a member of the president’s National Security Council.
But in all those years, I have never felt as much of a threat to our country, our Constitution, and our very democracy as I do right now. I said I would never run for office. But in this moment, I feel an obligation to step up, serve my community, and defend our country once again.
**I am running for Congress to defeat Lauren Boebert because when she was sworn into office, Lauren took a similar oath to defend our Constitution – and she has betrayed it almost every single day since then.**
Adam Frisch only lost to Lauren Boebert by 546 votes. It was the closest race in the entire country. We can finally put an end to Lauren Boebert’s embarrassing political career – but I need your help now to do it.
Our campaign needs to raise another $25,000 before our deadline at midnight to defeat Lauren Boebert and take back the House for Democrats, but right now, we’re still short. **If I am going to send Lauren Boebert packing and flip this seat blue, I need grassroots donors like you to chip in right now to my campaign:**

# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2210%2E791427%2EfG9ZTA)
Friend — Minnesota has an open race for Senate this year, and it’s a seat that Democrats absolutely must win if we want to take control of Congress.
**Today, I’m making my pick: I’m proud to endorse Minnesota Lt. Governor Peggy Flanagan’s campaign for United States Senate!**
[**If that’s all you need to hear, split a quick contribution between me and Peggy’s campaign to help power her grassroots efforts to Get Out the Vote! Otherwise, please read on:**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-flanagan.tyhTev&refcode=em260512-1-180&t=2&akid=2210%2E791427%2EfG9ZTA)
**[CONTRIBUTE](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-flanagan.tyhTev&refcode=em260512-1-180&t=3&akid=2210%2E791427%2EfG9ZTA)**
Peggy is a true progressive fighter who is ready to stand up to Donald Trump, take on corporate greed, and fight for working people and all communities across Minnesota.
When ICE came to Minnesota to harass and terrorize our communities, she didn’t back down. Peggy was on the front lines with me and our neighbors, organizing our response, protecting our constitutional rights, and connecting people with the resources they needed to stay safe. She showed real leadership at a time when Minnesota was under an unjust and politically-motivated occupation by federal agents.
She’s also proven her commitment to the fight against oligarchy and the billionaire class. If we send her to the Senate, Peggy will be a reliable vote in favor of Medicare-for-All, taxing the mega-wealthy, raising the minimum wage, banning corporate money in politics, and much more. That’s why she’s also been endorsed by progressive leaders across the country, such as Bernie Sanders, Elizabeth Warren, and Pramila Jayapal.
The bottom line is that Peggy Flanagan understands exactly what this moment demands: Leaders who are willing to speak with moral clarity, challenge the status quo, and fight unapologetically for working people.
[**If you’re with me and Peggy in the fight for a better future for Minnesota and all of America, split a contribution between my campaign and Peggy’s today. We have just a few months to organize for victory and send a true champion for working people to the Senate.**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-flanagan.tyhTev&refcode=em260512-1-180&t=4&akid=2210%2E791427%2EfG9ZTA)

You can help by making calls to voters. | | | Friend, with three weeks to go until the June 2 primary, we're running daily phone banks targeting Democratic voters, Democratic-leaning voters, and young people. The MAGA justices on John Roberts' Supreme Court just made it easier for opponents of voting rights to rig our elections — and not for the first time.
In their latest decision, these billionaire-backed justices gutted a key part of the Voting Rights Act, making it easier for state legislatures to draw up district maps that dilute the voting power of Black and brown communities. This is how they help politicians control election results before votes are even cast.
This is not normal. This is power being taken from us. For years, John Roberts and his fellow conservative justices have chipped away at voting rights, siding with billionaire interests and politicians who don’t want to compete for our votes. Now they’ve gone further — clearing the way for maps that decide who wins before Election Day .

#
Peter —
I just made a risky decision, and you deserve to know why.
In one of our internal strategy meetings, my team made the case that, if we made some earlier investments than we planned, it would have an outsized impact in November.
You see, right now, our Republican opponents and their dark-money backers are spending millions against each other in a bruising runoff.
While they are in a race to the bottom, trying to outdo each other’s extremism to impress Trump and his MAGA base, we have a head start.
These early investments can put us in the strongest position to flip this seat no matter who our opponent is.
So I gave them the green light to spend the money — even though we didn’t have it in our budget. I made the bet that, if I explained the stakes and made the case to you, enough people in this movement would step up to fill the gap.
So I need to ask:

And it’s exactly what Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry is trying to do right now. Early voting had already started when he issued an emergency executive order to suspend the congressional primaries. Louisianans were casting their ballots under a map which ensured that Black voters — about a third of the state’s population — would be free to elect the candidates of their choice in two out of six congressional districts. But the Supreme Court had just said states could rig new Jim Crow–style voting maps that effectively disenfranchise voters of color. And the governor couldn’t wait to take advantage of this golden opportunity to turn back the clock. Now Louisiana lawmakers are racing to draw new maps that could eliminate both congressional districts with fair representation for Black voters. subject: The fight for voting rights just got harder
body:
It’s that much more important to build grassroots momentum

---
N/A, The fight for the House just got harder. Last month, the Supreme Court practically gutted the Voting Rights Act, stripping away key protections for minority communities. And now, the Virginia Supreme Court has struck down our voter-approved maps. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131255757/620468900/-499535588?refcode=260512_dr_vra_img&ms=260512_dr_vra&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTM1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNDRhMTA2ZC0xNzRlLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=i5EFpfKaWz0xqx_2JrCEzuNA9cZVSyImPE7z6qJqFOE=) Southern states are already racing to redraw their districts in their favor. The state is actively redrawing its congressional map. After the SCOTUS ruling struck down the existing map, Republican Gov. The legislature (in regular session) is working on a new map that could eliminate one or both Democratic-held majority-Black districts. Alabama (currently 5R-2D): LIKELY +1 GOP
Republican Gov. Kay Ivey called a special legislative session (beginning early May) to redraw the congressional map. Officials hope to implement changes before the 2026 elections, targeting the two Democratic seats. Alabama also has a pending related appeal that could be affected.

Republican Gov. Bill Lee called a special legislative session (beginning early May) specifically to review and redraw the congressional map. The focus is breaking up the single Democratic-held district centered on majority-Black Memphis. This is one of the more advanced efforts among the states listed. The map was signed into law Friday.

Mississippi (currently 3R-1D): NO CHANGE
Gov. Tate Reeves called a special session for May 20, but it is limited to redistricting the state's Supreme Court (judicial) districts in response to a separate VRA-related case and the Callais ruling's impact on race-based districting standards. There is no active legislative push or special session focused on congressional districts for the 2026 elections. Some discussion of congressional changes has occurred informally, but timing and legal constraints make it unlikely the current map will change before November.

South Carolina (currently 6R-1D): POTENTIAL +1 GOP
The Republican-controlled House voted 87-27 on May 6-7 to approve a resolution allowing lawmakers to reconvene after the regular session ends and redraw the congressional map, explicitly targeting the majority-Black 6th District held by longtime Democratic Rep. Jim Clyburn. A new map could be introduced as soon as May 7-8, with committee hearings to follow. The proposal now requires Senate approval (two-thirds vote). Earlier statements from some GOP leaders called full redistricting this year "unlikely" due to timing, but the House action has advanced the effort. Primaries are approaching (around June), so any changes would face logistical and potential legal hurdles.

| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/jeffjacksonnc/p/two-good-wins?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

Over 100,000 people in NC need one of these:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/27c7f86f-218d-4e6c-896d-1389596dead3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This is an EpiPen. It's for people with severe allergic reactions, the kind you can die from.
If you feel a reaction starting, you're supposed to grab one, inject it into your thigh, and call 911. It's supposed to keep you alive until the ambulance arrives.
_**But:**_
The company that sells them, we believe, was breaking the law to keep prices high.
In 2007, a two-pack of EpiPens cost about $100 and by 2016, it was $600.
That's six times the price in nine years.
Here's how we believe they did it:
First, when a cheaper, generic version was about to hit the market, they paid the middlemen who decide which drugs get covered by insurance to keep the generic off the list. (PBMs strike again...)
Second, they used the patent system to delay competitors from even getting to market.
And third, they ran marketing campaigns making misleading claims about the generics that did exist.
The combined effect of all this meant less competition, which let them charge higher prices.
So we went to the company, Mylan, and said, "We think we have evidence you've been breaking the law and overcharging people in North Carolina, including the state itself."
And now we've announced an $11m dollar settlement with them. A chunk of money is going back to state taxpayers because a lot of these EpiPens were purchased with state money for people who otherwise couldn't have paid for them. That's why I'm standing with Treasurer Brad Briner in the photo above - the Treasurer runs the State Health Plan, which got a payment from our settlement.
Two important notes on this:
First, our $11m was just for NC, other states are doing their own lawsuits, and there was also a major class action lawsuit. So there's more accountability than just our effort.
Second, in addition to the $11m, the company must now lower out-of-pocket costs for people buying the generic version going forward - and that's for everyone across the country.
Good win.
### **Our big TV case**
I gave you first part of this story a month ago. Quick recap and then the latest.
The biggest TV company in America is called Nexstar.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/893ffbee-22fd-42c4-ba46-ab212ef0ef52?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
It owns about 200 stations, including Fox, ABC, CBS, and NBC affiliates all across the country.
Nexstar is trying to buy the third-biggest TV company, called Tegna.
The combined company would be - by far - the largest TV company in American history. It would reach 80% of American homes. No single company has ever controlled that much broadcast television.
In addition to giving one company enormous control over the local news Americans watch, the merger would also likely mean higher cable bills and layoffs in local newsrooms.
No big mystery how this would work.
Let's say Nexstar goes from owning your local Fox station to also owning your local CBS station. You would have fewer choices, so they could charge more. They would also have more people in the same area doing reporting, so they could cut back on reporters.
This is especially important to North Carolina because we'd be the _third-most impacted state_ in the country. Nexstar and Tegna both have a major presence here:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/edd9c4d9-0644-4a92-981d-aefef9dc5a96?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
There's a strong argument this is illegal media consolidation.
The federal government has a standard way of measuring whether a merger concentrates too much power in one company. When a merger pushes concentration past a certain threshold and increases it by more than 100 points, it's presumed illegal. In every single NC market affected by this deal, the merger doesn't just cross the legal threshold, it obliterates it:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/244b38d9-c84f-43b0-994c-495ee0300791?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So a few weeks ago, I joined a bipartisan coalition of AGs and we filed a lawsuit to block the merger.
_But then_ \- as I told you at the time - things took a turn.
The moment we filed our lawsuit, Nexstar hit the gas to try to close the deal before a court could stop them. Less than 24 hours after we filed, the FCC, which would normally block a merger like this, suddenly waived its rules and let it happen. Then USDOJ gave its approval.
For all of that to happen in 24 hours is very strange.
Then Nexstar tried to declare victory and said the deal was done.
So we filed an emergency motion that basically said: "Hey judge, they're trying to get around you. They know the law isn't on their side, and the last thing they want is for you to hear our case. That's exactly why you should. Let's hit pause before you let them become the biggest local TV company in American history."
Well, the judge just ruled, _and we won_ \- the emergency motion, not the whole case.
That means the court issued a preliminary injunction freezing the merger. Nexstar and Tegna have to keep operating as separate companies, with separate management and separate newsrooms, while our case plays out.
Now we get to make our full case, and we've got a strong one.
Another good win - but this case is just beginning.
All for now. Working on some interesting stuff to report to you next week.
Best,
Jeff Jackson

subject: If you love America, read this first
body:
We are closer to losing this country than most people are willing to admit.
_Please see a special message from our sponsor. If you would like to unsubscribe, visit this[link](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/s/u/LM36hyXArDCv6OHUij5LUqX3zcf5REHC8xaDjd8zrZ2yOXs1A31M9G-M8HKTfnLJZUYJxF95mHK5mY-hI-8FA8uPKW-x4YbpUHjSem63NXMl9sV7fO7uqNzCo_xi6ewLNKFP36qWmGydNxphyDSLzB1YxoYJVznwMd2ED5XBJP3Sl0kRm00GM-MH/zdqR1QtppwZcMOYdcNdN5ZU858jZLYlU/20)_
| | |
---
| | Peter,
---
I'm going to be blunt with you.

We are closer to losing this country than most people are willing to admit.

Not someday. Not "if things keep going this way."

Right now.

And the scariest part?

It's not happening in Washington. It's happening in classrooms.

High schools. Colleges.

Places where the next generation is being shaped -- or more accurately... reshaped.

If you've ever looked at what's coming out of our schools and thought: _" What happened to this country?" _

You're not wrong. You're seeing it clearly.

Because while most people are arguing online... while they're hoping things will turn around... while they're waiting for the next election to fix everything...

The other side is doing something far more dangerous.

They're raising the next generation.

Earlier. Faster. And with zero resistance in most places.

That's how countries are lost.

Slowly. Then all at once.

But here's the thing that should give a patriot like you hope...

There is one place where that trend is actually being challenged.

_And it shouldn 't even exist. _

**Just one year ago, Turning Point USA 's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools.**
That alone felt like a miracle.

Because starting even ONE chapter today takes courage most adults don't have.

Conservative students get mocked. Targeted. Threatened. Shut down.

And yet...

_They stepped up anyway. _

About that time, Charlie called me.

He didn't sound optimistic... He sounded urgent.

"Andrew, we've got to move faster."

I told him we were. He stopped me.

"No. You're not thinking what I'm thinking. I want to be in 35,000 high schools."

I actually laughed.

"Charlie... there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America."

"Okay," he said. "How many are there?"

"About 27,000."

And without hesitation: "Good. Let's do 27,000."

I remember sitting there thinking to myself... we're barely in 1,200 schools.

We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the infrastructure. We didn't even have the roadmap yet.

But Charlie wasn't fazed.

_" We'll figure it out." _

That was him.

He didn't wait for perfect conditions.

Because he knew something most people don't want to face: If we wait... _we lose everything. _

And now?

Less than a year later...
---
[](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/s/c/-m-9ligXTLTBk5xvctlirdmSGxLtU4J5JUrHgxwnYyCpbfkV2SsZbnq5CFZ2_NpQQApNPqBh2spTdgWo6-0Bi6k8IHAASXUSBYZXKTdWRJF0-l_XmUyXp0HZdVCG5guSdAGO9eh_nM6sRmaJ2_BZW80Qkv8V2cVrJV0xd8lZRcxdnEtN51KoDCStApLOBix7oN5q8vSwUdmNTGFqq1BjiFFHXRLXr3xQ2NoLgWrqF92L9aM-v14q_UMrNpSwyRHKcleDOiHcMtLprQEyPrFRGkY2uB0DCDmAnFNaZNTY28N-Uup_S29T5pklgMxnZRLB-D95FytMQ97aIOTdV5znndlpRdvAr8Z4MO6B1Nyz5zK052YzpmdOQgcTTUzf35kge72WlTmMwnetG5qJFOlwsNopU3TL2CabcazAzz4A5qyIG5Tc10nxwHDYZVJEkMgFYRx5GMSq5fV-tdJroo3CLvP_wrWvNWqBjXvUQVEeMeBWtqdhZOO2pnNtAHL1cOiGFAuwCGlkylXSVAOTf6ZuvTbe01N3DFiFHBaRd6lc2M7wfCQtQA1Li_hjnEHQg_4pxoT96_OZVWQ01XKD7tOllOKTsvY5vj59itz9NiqCanRRIGXkj9qxqcU6Z1nhw5bTqBN7MIWtd2kP7zn2uVePmHL7cMQuAaVUOOT9p66yWhbCiZwESsYqB5uZ8v-4F_yo1lWbBeQi7Pyh_2_M9w1o-8YwVnB6YQDZ7uvbEvyeBvycbBz-dmx-ooJPvm19/UyqHt-izTF0jB8pFwAYeQiVgAjzqS6RL/20)
---
**We 're in 3,300 schools. **

**Thirteen percent of all high schools in America. **

**Eight states are now backing this effort to put a Club America chapter in every high school statewide. **

_That shouldn 't be possible. _

Not in this environment. Not with the level of hostility these students face every single day.

And yet... it's still happening.

_But Peter, here 's the part you need to understand: _

This is not a victory. It's a foothold.

_Because in the other 87% of schools? _

There is no resistance. None.

Just one-sided propaganda from the Left.

One-sided pressure on kids who are too young to even realize what's happening to them.

That's the reality.

The question isn't whether we're fighting. We are.

The question is whether it's enough.

Because right now, the students stepping up through Club America...

They're not the majority. _They 're the exception. _

They're the ones willing to take the heat.

The ones willing to stand alone.

The ones willing to risk being targeted just to say: _" I love this country." _
---
[](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/s/c/K--pbPYEodvBSCpLKT9K4rpU_khRPEx7Gv-L_YQBox5243JyHZBaRc-bfX-m8cXpnOn9TElaXMer8XtEZbTD5D30bPOCWytjAOBA5icUw8-_HVzpad-a6EVmxH9RxRxt3Lg7DdVUp9ZGxrMu3p1sz_YSR5Q9ZAvFSnAJkRSKRGLg0R3oIY_Q9GkqKj4tsoAq11hB90mbKePwACnz-tf7NrKpjseBATPOzMhCOLRF9pgKPdQotGANn5xfnRhTzIAx3XNfW_cvWP3sD42Ew-2Y56EJV5SPnWseYUNOJqW94VIdIifJ6O324VjWydwhvKUXBXTAG0MiiHxI5yFkjYGZiNf8HRVad5R6amY4idSRIlrIM8xI9qNTg6ie-tAkTAOTnVE5W-aLZJZu-_DC7g3MCaT4RlwI__c8XxRs5eGAJy81TiOUr-jB4zwDJ8UC3e1838UcuVJHrcioQzRX7V01AkOw89czGGE2IkWk0GexuMMAio28Mbz8SBfkPpXXxVedQt9FGZX1kzLef2OM3LxlnGvxNID9hR7lq1Q-RFShHK7-VSgdvYwh2EsKaPIT0HfbzpzxJRJB59LHY02h7wHDliSusC0h_ZH1W6K543mQeoguanGu3ZzExL0MIDiN1D1Po7OttLEkZAuIwlZcY_vBp_bpikBmHE6G-J8vETBggAQgoZ_gaFb1Y52IFNgXxrVPyW4V9Sje0iRB-1VA9gS_meYswmtisKoJ-BIt_bmB_Ixqn4LwZHQb4YJx8n4F/p9FhRGItIuz1L0M65ANmBkZKevXV0Sg3/20)
---
And every time one of those students raises their hand...

We have a choice.

Back them. _Or leave them on their own. _

**Because when a student starts a chapter, we send them an activism kit -- with American flags. Pocket Constitutions. Leadership tools. **

Everything they need to actually stand their ground.

Not symbolically. For real.

They've already made the decision to lead.

All they're waiting on... is you and me.

**Each activism kit costs $25. That 's it. **

$25 to make sure one student doesn't have to stand alone against the Left in a hostile school.

I was falsely convicted of first degree murder and lost 28 years of my freedom.
| | | | | [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001Pux-zoCeD61MzIQ7UmrWSef-q4F_lMocWnPBTiMQeKECQEPaSTbXDY_sBZUxunrH8ZvcjKForGBM9lAUiQS-dF6vOs9ZFOs17wPUeSp4HptCX-sPnIZYQ-CrANbbFtshwyzhD4ohUoXKs1mD2AaezYTuzUT2TnI95-yQmdBuC9VU9QCnstACNAhl07MGCKNJMHVUgaxS-nMD_xeI5BW3GVjg73EJRC9IIkwq9TwtsbQ=&c=DL1D1pRp7LWHy2tIdA9HZqEjGGpomaoXQGf-cGEJOEcQHOmx1Em3bQ==&ch=wU47YzqXJvfIHA1la0DGPdSBndAVzH-T6uYMHbn30a1WfU0Z09pabA==)

| Peter,
My name is Calvin Duncan, and I served 28 years in prison for a crime I did not commit.
I was 19 years old when the police arrested me for murder. A single witness made a tentative cross-racial identification from a photo taken when I was 14. The two detectives who interrogated me were already under FBI investigation for fraud. And they lied to my jury about what I said in the interrogation.
I spent years in jail awaiting trial, where I faced the possibility of a death sentence. The whole time he represented me, my lawyer only came to see me once - the night before trial.
I only had an eighth grade education and no lawyer was coming to save me. So I did the only thing I could: I started teaching myself the law. At 21 years old, awaiting trial in a death penalty case, I filed my first motion. I called it a "Motion for a Law Book." The police lied on the stand, my jury convicted me, and I was sentenced to life without parole.
---
| [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001Pux-zoCeD61MzIQ7UmrWSef-q4F_lMocWnPBTiMQeKECQEPaSTbXDY_sBZUxunrH8ZvcjKForGBM9lAUiQS-dF6vOs9ZFOs17wPUeSp4HptCX-sPnIZYQ-CrANbbFtshwyzhD4ohUoXKs1mD2AaezYTuzUT2TnI95-yQmdBuC9VU9QCnstACNAhl07MGCKNJMHVUgaxS-nMD_xeI5BW3Gb1oNizQ8TNGfVlAVMSpd2o=&c=DL1D1pRp7LWHy2tIdA9HZqEjGGpomaoXQGf-cGEJOEcQHOmx1Em3bQ==&ch=wU47YzqXJvfIHA1la0DGPdSBndAVzH-T6uYMHbn30a1WfU0Z09pabA==)
---
A photo of me studying in the law library at the Louisiana State Penitentiary at Angola.
But instead of giving up, my faith in the Constitution and our laws only grew. As a jailhouse lawyer, I continued to fight my own case, and I helped thousands of people access the courts from prison. I sold my plasma to pay for court records. I kept fighting even when it seemed hopeless. And in 2011, with the help of the Innocence Project of New Orleans, I finally won my freedom after more than 28 years.
In 2021, Louisiana passed a new law that allowed people like me to present evidence that proved our factual innocence. I proved my case, the judge vacated my conviction and I was fully exonerated.
But I have never walked away from the fight for justice. I studied and got my law degree. And I ran for Orleans Parish Clerk of Criminal Court on one promise: I won't ever let what happened to me happen to anybody else.
And the people of New Orleans elected me with 68% of the vote. That was supposed to be the end of the story.
---
| [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001Pux-zoCeD61MzIQ7UmrWSef-q4F_lMocWnPBTiMQeKECQEPaSTbXDY_sBZUxunrH8ZvcjKForGBM9lAUiQS-dF6vOs9ZFOs17wPUeSp4HptCX-sPnIZYQ-CrANbbFtshwyzhD4ohUoXKs1mD2AaezYTuzUT2TnI95-yQmdBuC9VU9QCnstACNAhl07MGCKNJMHVUgaxS-nMD_xeI5BW3GQF5yH5Law7H6quzIwmThxk=&c=DL1D1pRp7LWHy2tIdA9HZqEjGGpomaoXQGf-cGEJOEcQHOmx1Em3bQ==&ch=wU47YzqXJvfIHA1la0DGPdSBndAVzH-T6uYMHbn30a1WfU0Z09pabA==)

MAGA has launched a coordinated assault on Black representation in Louisiana. At the urging of Louisiana's Governor, MAGA Senator Jay Morris introduced legislation to eliminate my office and it passed in the Republican controlled state legislature.
Morris is the same man who introduced new redistricting maps that threaten to wipe out our two majority-Black congressional districts in Louisiana after the Supreme Court gutted the Voting Rights Act. When he testified before the state legislature about those maps, he turned to a room full of Black elected leaders and told them "you need to shut up, boy" as he walked out of the chamber.
We are fighting back against MAGA's assault on Black representation.
And New Orleans' City Council has already proclaimed a special election to fill the seat Morris' legislation created when he tried to eliminate mine. I am not going anywhere.
I will keep fighting in court to resume the office I was already elected to. And if I need to run again, I will, to fulfill my promise to voters, to protect the integrity of our elections, and to make sure what happened to me never happens to anyone else. Gov. Landry and his lackeys like Jay Morris won't silence us.

The billionaires and tech bros have their super PACs, dark-money networks, and deep-pocketed donors.
We have something better: _people_.
People chipping in what they can because they believe our communities deserve better. People who know small towns are worth fighting for. People ready to help Democrats expand the map and fight for schools, jobs, healthcare, childcare, and the issues that shape people’s lives every day.

Peter,

**In a recent debate, I challenged my opponents to do something simple:_disclose all of their stock trades over the past decade._**

Connie Chan immediately agreed.
Saikat Chakrabarti - the borderline billionaire who has poured over $5 million of his own tech and private equity wealth into this race to buy this seat - **has been radio silent.**

That silence speaks volumes.

When politicians profit off the decisions they're making, voters lose. And San Franciscans should never have to wonder whether our leaders are putting us, or their profits first.

_That’s why we need to ban all members of Congress from trading stocks_ \- restoring the basic accountability and transparency our democracy depends on. And it's one of the first things I'll fight for in Washington.

Saikat Chakrabarti - the borderline billionaire who has poured over $5 million of his own tech and private equity wealth into this race to buy this seat - has been radio silent. That silence speaks volumes. When politicians profit off the decisions they're making, voters lose. Friend — Texas has one of the worst maternal healthcare crises in the country.
So lawmakers proposed something simple: a pilot program in Harris County to help pregnant women on Medicaid get better care and ensure healthier pregnancies.
Steve Toth voted against it.
Out of the entire legislature , he was just one of 12 lawmakers, Republicans included, to oppose it.
Yes, At a time when families are struggling and maternal healthcare in Texas is under enormous strain...
Steve Toth was against creating a women’s home pilot program designed to improve care for mothers and babies on Medicaid.
That vote says a lot about Steve Toth’s radical extremism and cruelty.
This is one of the reasons I’m running for Congress.

There’s a
name for what’s happening in the Trump administration right now, and it’s
not “merit-based hiring.”

It’s cronyism — shameless, pure, loyalty-first cronyism.

Because the fastest path to a federal judgeship or top DOJ job isn’t
public service or legal excellence anymore. It’s being Donald Trump’s
personal lawyer and proving your loyalty.

Since returning to office, Trump has elevated at least 10 of his former
personal attorneys into senior Justice Department roles or lifetime
judicial nominations.

Not career prosecutors. Not independent legal minds. His personal defense
team.

And a growing number of judicial nominees share the same defining
credential: loyalty proven in Trump’s own legal battles.

Let’s be clear: these aren’t neutral appointments. They’re rewards. And
they create an obvious conflict of interest — people who defended one man
now serving in roles that demand independence from him.

That’s not how a justice system is supposed to work. The DOJ isn’t a
president’s law firm. The federal judiciary isn’t a loyalty program. But
that’s how it’s being treated.

And the result is a pipeline from “Trump’s personal lawyer” to “lifetime
federal judge” — shaping the courts around allegiance, not independence.

We can’t normalize this. Demand Justice PAC is fighting to expose this
corruption, block the extremist nominees, and demand a judiciary that
answers to the Constitution, not to a wannabe authoritarian.

The recent defection of State Representative Nasif Majeed from the Democratic Party--following Representative Carla Cunningham's departure just days earlier--represents more than the disillusionment of two politicians. Majeed, who leaves the party saying simply "I didn't leave the Democratic Party. The Democratic Party left me," voted with Republicans to override Governor Josh Stein's veto of legislation concerning sexuality and religion in schools. His statement that he had "some moral issues and I had to lean on my values" tells the story of a party that has abandoned traditional Democratic principles in favor of radical ideology. Cunningham, after 14 years in the House, concluded that "being an independent thinker does not align with party politics."

Perhaps no issue better illustrates the institutional rot in North Carolina's election infrastructure than the recent discovery of approximately 34,000 deceased individuals on the state's voter rolls. This shocking revelation came after the Trump administration pursued legal action against North Carolina, forcing the State Board of Elections to perform actual database maintenance. The NCSBE, controlled by Democratic appointees, had to be sued by the federal government before taking action that federal law already required. Dr. Andy Jackson of the John Locke Foundation noted that the state removed 500,000 ineligible voters through standard biennial maintenance in 2025--raising the question: why did this process require federal intervention in the first place?

The dead voter scandal is only the latest chapter in North Carolina's election integrity nightmare. The infamous NC-9th District scandal of 2018, where political operative McCrae Dowless orchestrated an absentee ballot harvesting scheme for Republican candidate Mark Harris, resulted in a new election being ordered. Dowless illegally collected absentee ballots, forged signatures, and filled in votes for local candidates--activities that threw the entire election into question. More recently, the 2024 State Supreme Court race represented the last unresolved election in the nation, with Republican challenger Jefferson Griffin fighting over 60,000 ballots with incomplete registration records until finally conceding months after Election Day.

Perhaps most damning is the mounting evidence suggesting North Carolina's own University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill may be ground zero for the COVID-19 pandemic. Dr. Robert Redfield, former CDC Director under President Trump, has stated that UNC Chapel Hill's Ralph Baric--"the scientific mastermind" behind coronavirus research--was "very involved" in creating "original viral lines." Redfield claimed there is a "real possibility that the virus's birthplace was Chapel Hill."

Baric's lab at UNC spent decades conducting gain-of-function research on coronaviruses, research that continued long after federal moratoriums were supposed to restrict such dangerous experimentation. When SARS-related coronavirus genomes from the Wuhan Institute of Virology were sent to Baric's UNC lab, they were manipulated and studied--creating the exact type of chimeric viruses that could have escaped and caused the pandemic. The Obama administration failed to properly oversee this research. The Biden administration actively suppressed lab-leak investigations, with Dr. Anthony Fauci orchestrating the publication of papers dismissing the possibility--while knowing full well about Baric's work and the connections between UNC and Wuhan.

CaI rol Folt, before becoming a university administrator, built her career as a prominent environmental toxicologist who secured substantial federal research funding. At Dartmouth College, where she spent three decades rising from faculty to interim president, Folt was deeply embedded in NIH-funded research--serving as associate director of the $15 million NIEHS/EPA-funded Superfund Research Program studying toxic metals like arsenic and mercury, and later participating in the $8 million Children's Environmental Health and Disease Prevention Research Center jointly funded by the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS) and the EPA. When she was recruited away from UNC Chapel Hill to become president of the University of Southern California in 2019, she brought this extensive experience in federally funded scientific research with her. Today, USC continues to aggressively pursue NIH grants under her leadership--the university recently secured an $8 million NIH grant to establish the Southern California Center for Chronic Health Disparities in Environmental Exposure (ShARP Center) to study PFAS "forever chemicals," with Folt publicly championing such federal research partnerships as central to the university's mission.

North Carolina is fundamentally a Republican state--now explicitly so. For the first time in history, Republican voters officially outnumber registered Democrats. Since 2000, North Carolina has voted Democratic in only 14.3% of presidential elections while voting Republican 85.7% of the time. Donald Trump won North Carolina in all three of his presidential campaigns--the only candidate in the modern era to do so consistently.

Yet the state's Republican majority has been systematically undermined. Democratic Governor Roy Cooper, while presenting a moderate face, actively implemented the Biden administration's agenda--from embracing the regulatory burdens that drove up energy costs to supporting the open-border policies that strained state resources to pursuing COVID lockdowns long after the science justified them.

The Obama and Biden administrations treated North Carolina as a vassal state to be managed rather than a sovereign jurisdiction. When the state's voters elected Republican majorities and supported conservative policies, the federal government responded with lawsuits, investigations, and threats. The Department of Justice sued North Carolina over its voter rolls only after years of Republican pressure. The Environmental Protection Agency targeted the state's energy sector. The Department of Education attacked North Carolina's schools over bathroom policies.

Meanwhile, Democratic-aligned institutions from UNC to the state elections apparatus operated as extensions of the national party rather than servants of North Carolinians. The result has been a state with Republican voters, Republican representatives, and Republican presidential preferences--yet governed by Democratic appointees in key administrative positions and subjected to federal pressure whenever it attempted to assert its sovereignty.
Representatives Majeed and Cunningham's departure from the Democratic Party is symptomatic of a larger realignment. North Carolina's voters have made their preference clear through registration, voting patterns, and presidential preference. The scandals--dead voters on rolls, rigged congressional elections, and potentially world-altering biochemical research failures--reflect a state infrastructure captured by interests disconnected from its actual residents. The UNC-Chapel Hill COVID research scandal, in particular, suggests the grave consequences of this disconnect: federal funding priorities, academic ideology, and bureaucratic negligence combining to potentially unleash a global catastrophe.

North Carolina is red. Its people are red. Its problems stem from a Democratic establishment that refuses to accept this reality--and from federal administrations that used the state's institutions as testing grounds for failed policies. The exit of two Democratic legislators may be just the beginning.

Peter,
In the past few weeks, MAGA has unleashed a blitzkrieg in the courts. Two decisions in particular should send a chill down every American's spine.
Yesterday, the Supreme Court ruled that Alabama can suspend an ongoing election to rush through a gerrymandered map. This came after the same court threw out a challenge to Texas' illegal racially gerrymandered maps -- ruling it was too close to an election for the courts to intervene. That Texas decision came in December. Months before the primary.

**The McClatchy Media California editorial board endorsed Katie Porter for governor** after conducting interviews with every major Democratic candidate and Republican Steve Hilton. They called her “by far the most impressive” out of all the candidates.

Remember...
**Voting day is TUESDAY MAY 19TH!**
Bring a friend (or five) and get to the polls. Because the Republican Primary is the election that decides _what kind of Republican_ represents you.
» [Check your voter status here](https://substack.com/redirect/f3f9e56d-dd40-40dd-918a-ae8d3101bee9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Brian

Hey folks,
This one is bigger than partisan politics. Bigger than Democrat versus Republican. Bigger than the daily outrage cycle we all get trapped in.
A sitting Republican congressman just went on Tucker Carlson's show and basically admitted what a lot of people already suspect: there's a protected class of billionaires, political insiders, and powerful elites who think the rules simply do not apply to them -- and they're terrified of what happens if the Epstein files ever fully come out.
And honestly? The deeper you go down this rabbit hole, the uglier it gets.
**Here 's what we got into:**
* [**00:01:18**] Congressman Thomas Massie explains why the "Epstein class" operates above party politics -- and above accountability.
* [**00:02:29**] We get into the political retaliation happening against Republicans and Democrats who keep pushing for the files to be released.
* [**00:04:47**] Trump's alleged pressure campaign against allies speaking out on Epstein starts to come into focus.
* [**00:07:20**] Why this cover-up makes a lot more sense once you understand who's protecting whom -- and what's at stake for the billionaire class.
* [**00:15:23**] The core argument of this entire video: why none of our biggest problems get solved until this corrupt system of wealth and impunity is broken.

At the end of the day, this conversation isn't really about conspiracy theories or internet drama. It's about power. It's about whether wealthy, politically connected people can traffic in corruption, abuse, intimidation, and lies without ever facing consequences. And it's about whether ordinary people are finally reaching the point where we stop accepting it.
You don't have to agree with Thomas Massie or Tucker Carlson on everything to recognize that something deeply broken is happening here. This system protects itself. That's the point. And until we confront that reality head-on, nothing changes.

# **The Capitalist exists because of you, and we want to hear from you!**
**[Become a paid subscriber today and access the Live Capitalist chat](https://substack.com/redirect/4a7fa95a-7131-4166-983a-28a3b668810c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ Subscribe here now](https://substack.com/redirect/4a7fa95a-7131-4166-983a-28a3b668810c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
* * *
Call it what it is: **the rubber-meets-road moment for artificial intelligence.**
AI was the number-one draft pick, selected amid deafening fanfare and promises of future generational dominance, has finally been told to leave the bench and get on the field. No more standing on the sideline collecting cheers for future glory.
**It 's game time. **
**Produce.**
**Win.**
Or watch the crowd turn.
The sun is setting on the free-money era for AI. Not with a whimper, but with the unmistakable thud of lenders grumbling and balance sheets cracking under their own weight. For half a decade the sector has gorged itself on dreams and debt, valuations detached from **anything so pedestrian as actual cash returns.** Now the tabs for that venture are arriving and even the biggest names in the world are starting to sweat.
Oracle gave the rest of the industry a preview they cannot ignore. In December 2025 the software giant watched a $10 billion Michigan data center project, its flagship bet on the AI gold rush, stall when private lender Blue Owl Capital abruptly pulled financing. Shares cratered more than 5 percent in a session, part of an 18 percent monthly drop and a nearly 50 percent wipeout from September highs. Lease commitments had ballooned to $248 billion. Total debt topped $111 billion. Credit default swaps spiked to levels unseen since the 2009 crisis. This was no isolated hiccup. It was the sound of easy capital hitting a wall.
The AI boom lived well on that diet of dreams and debt and grew massively off the back of it. Hyperscalers issued press releases, signed 15- and 19-year leases, and projected $100 billion cloud empires while outsourcing the actual financing risk to pension funds and private lenders. They kept the equity clean, the story pristine, the stock prices elevated. But dreams do not service debt. And debt, eventually, demands payment.
At it's core the math in the minds of the hyperscalers was always a brutal zero sum game. Some one, we don't know who yet, will "crack" AI. A model will arrive one day that changes the game for everyone in the world forever, and who ever owns it will be the defacto leader in AI. They will be the Facebook to the industry's Myspace. This is the hyperscalers north star and they will spend any amount of money, take on any debt, even mortgage their future to the hilt, to stay at this high stakes table for a chance at being that winner.
But now the biggest players on earth are reaching the outer limits of what they can fund. Today's data from the AI arms race confirms it: capital expenditures are devouring operating cash flow from the richest players in the world at an alarming clip. Amazon is spending nearly every dollar it generates from its core business just to keep the infrastructure machine running. Meta and Alphabet sit not far behind. Microsoft's ratio climbs steadily higher. Push past 100 percent and the cash engine itself starts coughing.
Alphabet offers the sharpest picture of the trade-off. For years it traded like the ultimate cash machine, powered by search and advertising. Now its forward **[price-to-free-cash-flow multiple](https://substack.com/redirect/6fdf83c3-5bee-4910-aced-d231d0bf15f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** has rocketed above 200 times. Investors are paying premium prices for AI upside while the actual free cash flow--the money left after the build-out--gets squeezed to the bone.
The market is still betting on the dream. **The balance sheet is already living the reality.**

Hantavirus? 8 cases on a cruise ship.

[>>Watch his warning HERE<<](https://substack.com/redirect/0ba16022-6d28-4dbb-9c63-96cecdcae71c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

P.S. 600,000 mostly older Americans will die this year from the "Second Plandemic." No headlines. No WHO alerts. Just silence--**and profits.** **[See the proof.](https://substack.com/redirect/0ba16022-6d28-4dbb-9c63-96cecdcae71c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
* * *
* * *
Investor disquiet at Meta has been simmering for months. Billions spent on AI infrastructure, yet the returns remain stubbornly invisible. Boards and analysts have begun asking the uncomfortable question: how much longer can we fund this without proof? The ripples have now reached Google. The same pattern repeats across the hyperscalers. Capex is no longer a line item; it is the story. Thats not to say that the book is ending, but the story is running out of easy chapters.
## [Late, under fire, and running out of investor patience, Facebook's "Muse AI" cannot fail](https://substack.com/redirect/7f12e29f-2bf4-46e8-b6cf-b004bc3cbe9e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Oracle's situation is rapidly becoming the situation a lot of other AI giants are going to have to face. The company relied on off-balance-sheet leases and external partners precisely because its own cash flows could not shoulder the load. When one partner balked, the entire edifice trembled. Hidden leverage, long-term obligations, refinancing risk in a higher-rate world--these are no longer abstract concerns for startups. They are concrete problems for names the market once considered bulletproof. The canary in the coal mine just sang its loudest note yet.
## [Oracle's tumble is a warning for investors they should heed](https://substack.com/redirect/b0e62a16-1b21-4473-a213-db6e9cf77158?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
