| December 21, 2025
[](https://substack.com/redirect/b0e62a16-1b21-4473-a213-db6e9cf77158?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[](https://substack.com/redirect/b0e62a16-1b21-4473-a213-db6e9cf77158?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/b0e62a16-1b21-4473-a213-db6e9cf77158?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This is not the death of AI. That would be hysterical nonsense. The technology is real. The potential remains enormous. What is dying is the era of consequence-free capital investment. The era when you could announce a gigawatt-scale data center, slap an AI label on it, and watch the stock price levitate without anyone demanding a credible path to payback. That era relied on the polite fiction that efficiency gains and adoption curves would magically outrun the interest payments. The polite fiction is over.
## [The AI Boom's Fragile Foundations ](https://substack.com/redirect/eb329a21-442c-4731-9b73-6565d332fca5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [The Capitalist](https://substack.com/profile/333697867-the-capitalist)| | *
---|---|---
| October 4, 2025
[](https://substack.com/redirect/eb329a21-442c-4731-9b73-6565d332fca5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[In the late summer of 2025, Oracle's stock surged 25%, propelled by a single announcement: a $60 billion annual deal to provide cloud computing for OpenAI, the creator of ChatGPT.](https://substack.com/redirect/eb329a21-442c-4731-9b73-6565d332fca5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/eb329a21-442c-4731-9b73-6565d332fca5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Skeptics have warned for years that the data-center model itself sits on shaky ground. Billion-dollar facilities built for today's models could be obsolete tomorrow as AI technology improves at breakneck speed. Equipment depreciates faster than concrete. Long-term leases turn out to be riddled with escape clauses. Hyperscalers, for all their trillion-dollar market caps, have been remarkably reluctant to own the bricks and servers outright. They prefer to push the risk onto others while keeping the upside. The game was always clearer to those paying attention: "You build it. You finance it. We'll use it--until something better comes along."
When Oracle stumbled, the Nasdaq felt it. Chipmakers, suppliers, and fellow AI-exposed names moved in sympathy. Concentration risk in the S&P 500's top ten has never been higher. Bad news for one player now infects the entire ecosystem because investor psychology still ties them all together under the single banner of "AI." That banner is fraying.
For years the narrative was boundless opportunity, once-in-a-generation transformation, exponential growth that justified any multiple. Today the conversation has shifted, quietly but unmistakably, to balance-sheet health, refinancing risk, and whether the spending will ever translate into free cash flow that actually accrues to shareholders. Dreams do not pay dividends. Results do.
AI must now prove it belongs on the field. It must generate the returns that justify the hundreds of billions already committed and the hundreds of billions still to come. It must do so in an environment where capital is no longer free, where lenders ask harder questions, and where investors have grown tired of waiting for the payoff that was always "just around the corner."
The free-money era is closing because economic reality has a way of reasserting itself. Oracle revealed the hidden knowledge its name once promised: the AI boom's foundations were never as solid as the hype suggested. The giants are next in line to confront the same truth. They will not be spared by size or reputation.
**The bench is empty. The game is on. And the scoreboard does not lie.**

Shares cratered more than 5 percent in a session, part of an 18 percent monthly drop and a nearly 50 percent wipeout from September highs. Lease commitments had ballooned to $248 billion. Total debt topped $111 billion. Credit default swaps spiked to levels unseen since the 2009 crisis. This was no isolated hiccup. It was the sound of easy capital hitting a wall. The AI boom lived well on that diet of dreams and debt and grew massively off the back of it. Hyperscalers issued press releases, signed 15- and 19-year leases, and projected $100 billion cloud empires while outsourcing the actual financing risk to pension funds and private lenders. They kept the equity clean, the story pristine, the stock prices elevated. But dreams do not service debt. And debt, eventually, demands payment. At it's core the math in the minds of the hyperscalers was always a brutal zero sum game. Some one, we don't know who yet, will "crack" AI. A model will arrive one day that changes the game for everyone in the world forever, and who ever owns it will be the defacto leader in AI. They will be the Facebook to the industry's Myspace. This is the hyperscalers north star and they will spend any amount of money, take on any debt, even mortgage their future to the hilt, to stay at this high stakes table for a chance at being that winner. But now the biggest players on earth are reaching the outer limits of what they can fund. Today's data from the AI arms race confirms it: capital expenditures are devouring operating cash flow from the richest players in the world at an alarming clip. Amazon is spending nearly every dollar it generates from its core business just to keep the infrastructure machine running. Meta and Alphabet sit not far behind. Microsoft's ratio climbs steadily higher. Push past 100 percent and the cash engine itself starts coughing. Alphabet offers the sharpest picture of the trade-off. For years it traded like the ultimate cash machine, powered by search and advertising. Now its forward has rocketed above 200 times. Investors are paying premium prices for AI upside while the actual free cash flow--the money left after the build-out--gets squeezed to the bone. The market is still betting on the dream. The balance sheet is already living the reality. Sponsored by: Hantavirus isn't the pandemic. THIS is. Hantavirus? 8 cases on a cruise ship. | | ---|---|--- The REAL 1,700 deaths. Every. Single. Day. One is all over the news. The other is being buried. This MAHA doctor knows why. P.S. 600,000 mostly older Americans will die this year from the "Second Plandemic." No headlines. No WHO alerts. Just silence--and profits. Investor disquiet at Meta has been simmering for months. Billions spent on AI infrastructure, yet the returns remain stubbornly invisible. Boards and analysts have begun asking the uncomfortable question: how much longer can we fund this without proof? The ripples have now reached Google. The same pattern repeats across the hyperscalers. Capex is no longer a line item; it is the story. Thats not to say that the book is ending, but the story is running out of easy chapters. | | | | ---|---|--- | Apr 10 | Oracle's situation is rapidly becoming the situation a lot of other AI giants are going to have to face. The company relied on off-balance-sheet leases and external partners precisely because its own cash flows could not shoulder the load. When one partner balked, the entire edifice trembled. Hidden leverage, long-term obligations, refinancing risk in a higher-rate world--these are no longer abstract concerns for startups. They are concrete problems for names the market once considered bulletproof. The canary in the coal mine just sang its loudest note yet. | | | | ---|---|--- | December 21, 2025 | This is not the death of AI. That would be hysterical nonsense. The technology is real. The potential remains enormous. What is dying is the era of consequence-free capital investment. The era when you could announce a gigawatt-scale data center, slap an AI label on it, and watch the stock price levitate without anyone demanding a credible path to payback. That era relied on the polite fiction that efficiency gains and adoption curves would magically outrun the interest payments. The polite fiction is over. | | | | ---|---|--- | October 4, 2025 | Skeptics have warned for years that the data-center model itself sits on shaky ground. Billion-dollar facilities built for today's models could be obsolete tomorrow as AI technology improves at breakneck speed. Equipment depreciates faster than concrete. Long-term leases turn out to be riddled with escape clauses. Hyperscalers, for all their trillion-dollar market caps, have been remarkably reluctant to own the bricks and servers outright. They prefer to push the risk onto others while keeping the upside. The game was always clearer to those paying attention: "You build it. You finance it. We'll use it--until something better comes along." When Oracle stumbled, the Nasdaq felt it. Chipmakers, suppliers, and fellow AI-exposed names moved in sympathy. Concentration risk in the S&P 500's top ten has never been higher. Bad news for one player now infects the entire ecosystem because investor psychology still ties them all together under the single banner of "AI." That banner is fraying. For years the narrative was boundless opportunity, once-in-a-generation transformation, exponential growth that justified any multiple. Today the conversation has shifted, quietly but unmistakably, to balance-sheet health, refinancing risk, and whether the spending will ever translate into free cash flow that actually accrues to shareholders. Dreams do not pay dividends. Results do. AI must now prove it belongs on the field. It must generate the returns that justify the hundreds of billions already committed and the hundreds of billions still to come. It must do so in an environment where capital is no longer free, where lenders ask harder questions, and where investors have grown tired of waiting for the payoff that was always "just around the corner." The free-money era is closing because economic reality has a way of reasserting itself. Oracle revealed the hidden knowledge its name once promised: the AI boom's foundations were never as solid as the hype suggested. The giants are next in line to confront the same truth. They will not be spared by size or reputation. The bench is empty. The game is on. And the scoreboard does not lie. | Dear Peter, I have never been more sure of the power of community. This past weekend I canvassed with dozens of volunteers in Mission Viejo and Menifee, while other supporters set up sign brigades all over District 40. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. name: Isner for Alabama
subject: Alabama will not go quietly
body:
Voting rights rally Saturday in Montgomery!

| | | | | |
---
| | | | | |
Over the last two weeks, Alabama Republicans — backed by decisions from the U.S. Supreme Court — have continued efforts to weaken federal voting rights protections and implement maps that benefit them, regardless of the harm they do to democratic principles.
I know many people are confused and concerned about what all this means, so I want to be clear: The legal fight is not over. Voting will continue as scheduled on May 19, and voters should absolutely still show up and make their voices heard **on every single race**.
Governor Ivey just called a Special Primary for August 11 for Congressional Districts 1, 2, 6, and 7. If that is allowed by the courts, voters in those districts will have to vote again in August. But if the courts stop that Special Primary, the results of the May 19 primary for Congress will stand, so it's critical you vote on May 19.
The Special Primary that Governor Ivey just called for August 11 does not include State Senate districts 25 & 26\. A ruling on those districts may come quickly or may take months –– the timing is uncertain and up to the courts.
The truth is, we do not know how far these courts will go, nor how fast. We don't know which injunctions or rulings will ultimately remain in place and which will fall. But we do know this: educating and engaging voters in Alabama has never been more important.
And that's what we're going to keep doing. Day after day –– knocking doors, ringing phones, and talking to voters about the importance of voting. Because what’s at stake for Alabama has never been clearer.
So please: Keep speaking out. Keep organizing. Keep showing up. And if you’re able, please continue [supporting our campaign](https://us.list-manage.com/aEJPqGzkpCP?e=62156fa6a8&c2id=b6a5a472a55a2c2f8f90113ea210fcd0) as we continue to work tirelessly to ensure every Alabamian’s voice is heard and respected.
Forever loud,
Tabitha K. Isner
**NOTE: In light of the seriousness of this situation, we are postponing our previously scheduled event on Saturday in Wetumpka in favor of joining the National Day of Action for Voting Rights. We hope you can join us or do something in your own community to bring attention to the plight of the South.**

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131266905/620505128/1328794144?refcode=ea.b6ff7a22-2b4e-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ms=ea.b6ff7a22-2b4e-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImI2ZmY3YTIyLTJiNGUtZjExMS04ZWYyLTAwMGQzYTE0YjY0MCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=hfMI6ZvN8i6N1Do3UC6BoMggAvXp67A_3zN_oWxkzoE=&emci=b1ff7a22-2b4e-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=b6ff7a22-2b4e-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=4823105)

There's something profound you feel when you're alone in the wilderness. I've felt it listening to meadowlarks and mourning doves in the California hills of my childhood. I've felt it climbing high into the mountains. I've even felt it spending an unexpected night alone in Sequoia National Park in the 80s, where I realized how small we are in nature's presence. That connection to nature fuels my climate activism today. So when I see the Trump administration gutting the Endangered Species Act — which exists to protect vulnerable wildlife from extinction in the first place — in service of Big Oil and corporate special interests, it truly hurts my heart. They’re turning their backs on the very ecosystems and species we can’t live without. **[With Endangered Species Day coming up on May 15th, I want to hear directly from JanePAC supporters. Why does protecting endangered species and fighting extinction matter to YOU?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131266906/620505129/-581571288?refcode=ea.b6ff7a22-2b4e-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ms=ea.b6ff7a22-2b4e-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImI2ZmY3YTIyLTJiNGUtZjExMS04ZWYyLTAwMGQzYTE0YjY0MCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=hfMI6ZvN8i6N1Do3UC6BoMggAvXp67A_3zN_oWxkzoE=&emci=b1ff7a22-2b4e-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=b6ff7a22-2b4e-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=4823105)** | [**MESSAGE JANE →**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131266907/620505130/-581571288?refcode=ea.b6ff7a22-2b4e-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ms=ea.b6ff7a22-2b4e-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImI2ZmY3YTIyLTJiNGUtZjExMS04ZWYyLTAwMGQzYTE0YjY0MCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=hfMI6ZvN8i6N1Do3UC6BoMggAvXp67A_3zN_oWxkzoE=&emci=b1ff7a22-2b4e-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=b6ff7a22-2b4e-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=4823105)

It could be because you understand the importance of protecting animals like bald eagles, gray wolves, and grizzly bears. Or because you oppose the Trump administration’s attempt at giving oil and gas companies a “free pass” from protecting endangered species in the Gulf of Mexico. Maybe you just believe that all beings deserve a safe and healthy planet.
**There's no right or wrong answer. Whatever drives you, I want to hear it.**
**[Will you take a moment to share your story with me about why protecting endangered species matters to you? body:
The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great.

| | | [](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkbuO3SAQhp8Gdz7iYmxTUEQ6crcpokgp0RiGY7QGEy6b14-82RdIO_PPJ33z_3ozbxDOkF7fIaIuzZtSTTtCDfWAnDGF9PJQG5Z2QDKc8nmkcmT8zrHBaWcdMDugZsuyznRVbB0OPa3AcVGTnP0kZ7kjLnIVyOiuLLd2GYK-UVQyzlbK5PTwXqHcYQWFfoeJk4nCiaU9Cua-n8FCalDf_VUsPuwVh1MfreVKxDfCN8K3irYXfEBCd7U7QfjWerkFxnyF1MZegfBtUdLvcsFRoRLjhA5GhShG8Kv3EhnOCERs9erForGXQyKeP35ujAquGOFzb9FEdKFHIp4YIZxfw38nRDwPKA7quwH7-2tlIWYIr0TEs-VewYBt4SPU-PnRoWiX_4TzDHVeyERfN_RTsv1_JR-a_w0AAP__vlubyA)

| | Friend,
---
I want to give you a picture of what's really happening right now -- not the polished version, but what it actually looks like on the ground.

Inside our office, tables are covered in supplies and open boxes. Coworkers are coming together, packing materials, sealing kits, and sending them out the door as fast as possible.
---
[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkbuO3SAQhp8Gdz7iYmxTUEQ6crcpokgp0RiGY7QGEy6b14-82RdIO_PPJ33z_3ozbxDOkF7fIaIuzZtSTTtCDfWAnDGF9PJQG5Z2QDKc8nmkcmT8zrHBaWcdMDugZsuyznRVbB0OPa3AcVGTnP0kZ7kjLnIVyOiuLLd2GYK-UVQyzlbK5PTwXqHcYQWFfoeJk4nCiaU9Cua-n8FCalDf_VUsPuwVh1MfreVKxDfCN8K3irYXfEBCd7U7QfjWerkFxnyF1MZegfBtUdLvcsFRoRLjhA5GhShG8Kv3EhnOCERs9erForGXQyKeP35ujAquGOFzb9FEdKFHIp4YIZxfw38nRDwPKA7quwH7-2tlIWYIr0TEs-VewYBt4SPU-PnRoWiX_4TzDHVeyERfN_RTsv1_JR-a_w0AAP__vlubyA)
---
_Above: Activism kits bound for new chapters being packed with Constitutions, chapter handbooks, American flags, and more at TPUSA HQ in Arizona_
---
These boxes aren't sitting around waiting for someone to need them.

They're already claimed. And we don't have extras.

By the time one batch goes out, more requests come in.

Different schools, different students, same situation -- they want to start something, and they're asking us to help them do it.

That's where things stand right now.

We have more students stepping up than we can fully support at the moment.

And I don't say that lightly.

Because for years, the challenge wasn't getting students the tools -- it was getting them to speak up at all. Most kept their heads down.

The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great.

And for a long time, it worked. But that's all changing.

Now, we're seeing students stand up and push back.

**We saw it clearly at Wheeling High School in the Chicago suburbs -- Charlie's alma mater. **

For the first time, students there launched a Club America chapter. It took months to get approved, but a chapter is finally there.

And now, students are standing outside with signs about free markets and freedom -- not because it's easy, but because they've decided it matters more than staying quiet.
---
[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkbuO3SAQhp8Gdz7iYmxTUEQ6crcpokgp0RiGY7QGEy6b14-82RdIO_PPJ33z_3ozbxDOkF7fIaIuzZtSTTtCDfWAnDGF9PJQG5Z2QDKc8nmkcmT8zrHBaWcdMDugZsuyznRVbB0OPa3AcVGTnP0kZ7kjLnIVyOiuLLd2GYK-UVQyzlbK5PTwXqHcYQWFfoeJk4nCiaU9Cua-n8FCalDf_VUsPuwVh1MfreVKxDfCN8K3irYXfEBCd7U7QfjWerkFxnyF1MZegfBtUdLvcsFRoRLjhA5GhShG8Kv3EhnOCERs9erForGXQyKeP35ujAquGOFzb9FEdKFHIp4YIZxfw38nRDwPKA7quwH7-2tlIWYIr0TEs-VewYBt4SPU-PnRoWiX_4TzDHVeyERfN_RTsv1_JR-a_w0AAP__vlubyA)
---
That's not something you can just manufacture. But it is something you can support when it happens.

And it's not isolated growth anymore.

**We 're now working with more than 1,450 college chapters and over 3,400 high school chapters across the country. That's real scale. **

But if you zoom out, there are roughly 27,000 high schools in America.

That means tens of thousands of campuses where the Left still dominates the conversation...

And where students are waiting for someone to help them stand up and speak.

So as much as this has grown, we're still in the early innings of what Charlie actually set out to build.

What's different now is the pace.

**Many states are moving to bring Club America chapters to every high school statewide, including: **

✅ Arkansas
✅ Florida
✅ Idaho
✅ Indiana
✅ Montana
✅ Nebraska
✅ Oklahoma
✅ South Carolina
✅ Texas
✅ Tennessee

That brings us to ten states now taking this seriously -- not just talk, but action.
---
[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkbuO3SAQhp8Gdz7iYmxTUEQ6crcpokgp0RiGY7QGEy6b14-82RdIO_PPJ33z_3ozbxDOkF7fIaIuzZtSTTtCDfWAnDGF9PJQG5Z2QDKc8nmkcmT8zrHBaWcdMDugZsuyznRVbB0OPa3AcVGTnP0kZ7kjLnIVyOiuLLd2GYK-UVQyzlbK5PTwXqHcYQWFfoeJk4nCiaU9Cua-n8FCalDf_VUsPuwVh1MfreVKxDfCN8K3irYXfEBCd7U7QfjWerkFxnyF1MZegfBtUdLvcsFRoRLjhA5GhShG8Kv3EhnOCERs9erForGXQyKeP35ujAquGOFzb9FEdKFHIp4YIZxfw38nRDwPKA7quwH7-2tlIWYIr0TEs-VewYBt4SPU-PnRoWiX_4TzDHVeyERfN_RTsv1_JR-a_w0AAP__vlubyA)
---
That kind of expansion doesn't happen slowly.

It stacks quickly -- and it creates pressure behind the scenes to keep up.

Because every new chapter, every new student leader, every new school means more materials, more support, more follow-through.

And right now, that's where we're stretched.

We're not lacking interest or momentum.

We're working to keep up with both.

_So here 's how you can help... _

Right now, there are students ready to step up -- they just need the tools to do it.

**An activism kit puts everything they need directly into their hands: **

✅ Constitutions.
✅ Chapter guides.
✅ Flags.
✅ Materials to organize and lead.

It turns a student who wants to speak up... _into one who actually does. _

And you'll make it possible for us to keep saying yes when a student reaches out and says, "I want to start something here."

**[Each activism kit costs $25 to pack and ship to a student chapter. Will you put one into a student's hands today?](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkbuO3SAQhp8Gdz7iYmxTUEQ6crcpokgp0RiGY7QGEy6b14-82RdIO_PPJ33z_3ozbxDOkF7fIaIuzZtSTTtCDfWAnDGF9PJQG5Z2QDKc8nmkcmT8zrHBaWcdMDugZsuyznRVbB0OPa3AcVGTnP0kZ7kjLnIVyOiuLLd2GYK-UVQyzlbK5PTwXqHcYQWFfoeJk4nCiaU9Cua-n8FCalDf_VUsPuwVh1MfreVKxDfCN8K3irYXfEBCd7U7QfjWerkFxnyF1MZegfBtUdLvcsFRoRLjhA5GhShG8Kv3EhnOCERs9erForGXQyKeP35ujAquGOFzb9FEdKFHIp4YIZxfw38nRDwPKA7quwH7-2tlIWYIr0TEs-VewYBt4SPU-PnRoWiX_4TzDHVeyERfN_RTsv1_JR-a_w0AAP__vlubyA)**

clean_body: The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great. | | | | | Friend, I want to give you a picture of what's really happening right now -- not the polished version, but what it actually looks like on the ground. Inside our office, tables are covered in supplies and open boxes. Coworkers are coming together, packing materials, sealing kits, and sending them out the door as fast as possible. Above: Activism kits bound for new chapters being packed with Constitutions, chapter handbooks, American flags, and more at TPUSA HQ in Arizona These boxes aren't sitting around waiting for someone to need them. They're already claimed. And we don't have extras. By the time one batch goes out, more requests come in. Different schools, different students, same situation -- they want to start something, and they're asking us to help them do it. That's where things stand right now. We have more students stepping up than we can fully support at the moment. And I don't say that lightly. Because for years, the challenge wasn't getting students the tools -- it was getting them to speak up at all. Most kept their heads down. The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great. And for a long time, it worked. But that's all changing. Now, we're seeing students stand up and push back. We saw it clearly at Wheeling High School in the Chicago suburbs -- Charlie's alma mater. For the first time, students there launched a Club America chapter. It took months to get approved, but a chapter is finally there. And now, students are standing outside with signs about free markets and freedom -- not because it's easy, but because they've decided it matters more than staying quiet. That's not something you can just manufacture. But it is something you can support when it happens. And it's not isolated growth anymore. We 're now working with more than 1,450 college chapters and over 3,400 high school chapters across the country. That's real scale. But if you zoom out, there are roughly 27,000 high schools in America. That means tens of thousands of campuses where the Left still dominates the conversation... And where students are waiting for someone to help them stand up and speak. So as much as this has grown, we're still in the early innings of what Charlie actually set out to build. What's different now is the pace. Many states are moving to bring Club America chapters to every high school statewide, including: ✅ Arkansas ✅ Florida ✅ Idaho ✅ Indiana ✅ Montana ✅ Nebraska ✅ Oklahoma ✅ South Carolina ✅ Texas ✅ Tennessee That brings us to ten states now taking this seriously -- not just talk, but action. That kind of expansion doesn't happen slowly. It stacks quickly -- and it creates pressure behind the scenes to keep up. Because every new chapter, every new student leader, every new school means more materials, more support, more follow-through. And right now, that's where we're stretched. We're not lacking interest or momentum. We're working to keep up with both. So here 's how you can help... Right now, there are students ready to step up -- they just need the tools to do it. An activism kit puts everything they need directly into their hands: ✅ Constitutions. ✅ Chapter guides. ✅ Flags. ✅ Materials to organize and lead. It turns a student who wants to speak up... into one who actually does. And you'll make it possible for us to keep saying yes when a student reaches out and says, "I want to start something here." Every activism kit you help sponsor means one more student is ready to lead instead of sitting on the sidelines. That's how we keep saying "yes" when the next student steps forward. That's how this movement actually scales. Because the reality is, the demand is here now. The only question is whether we're equipped to meet it. clean_body: Republicans could call a constitutional convention without a single Democratic vote | = Peter, We know Republicans are working to destroy our fundamental freedoms from every angle. They're banning abortion, attacking IVF, and, based on rumblings from certain Republican-controlled legislatures, coming for birth control next. They're radically reshaping our courts and destroying our federal workforce. They're flouting foundational American ideals in order to fashion the current president into an unstoppable tyrant. They've made it clear, in other words, that their goal is to attack the very root of what defines America. And there's one plan of attack that doesn't get enough attention: The Republican plot to rewrite the U.S. Constitution. You read that right: If the GOP controls enough state legislatures, they can call a constitutional convention and rewrite our country's founding document. = | = Republicans have been working for decades to overwhelm state legislatures and rewrite the rules to ensure they stay in power at all costs. 28 states have already pledged to call for a constitutional convention, which means Republicans need to convince just SIX more to enshrine their anti-choice, anti-democracy ideas into our Constitution. I'm here to tell you we won't let that happen. We've been working to build governing majorities in critical states for decades, because we know that state legislatures are vital in protecting our rights. This cycle is no different: we have strong Democratic pro-choice women running at the state level in 2026. If you ever doubted we could win America's youth back from the Left...

If you ever wondered whether we'd lost the next generation for good...

If you ever sat up at night -- watching the news, seeing what's happening in our schools, our culture, our country -- and thought, _" Is it already too late?" _

You're not alone.

A lot of good people have been asking the same question.

**But I want to tell you something that might just change how you feel about the future of this country... **

Just one year ago, Turning Point USA's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools.

That was no small feat.

Starting a single chapter today takes serious courage. Students get mocked. Threatened. Investigated. Sometimes even physically attacked.

So reaching 1,200 chapters already felt like a miracle.

_Then Charlie called me... _

He said: "Andrew, I love what we're doing with our high school program -- but we've got to move faster."

I told him, "We are."

Charlie replied, "No you're not thinking what I'm thinking... I want to be in 35,000 high schools."

I laughed. I told him, "Charlie, there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America."

"Okay," he said, "How many are there?"

"About 27,000."

Without skipping a beat, Charlie said, "Okay, great. Let's do 27,000!"
I'll be honest -- I froze.

We didn't have the numbers. We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the roadmap yet.

But he wasn't fazed.

He said, "Don't worry. We'll figure it out. We'll do it together."

That was Charlie.

He didn't think small. He didn't move slow. He didn't settle for "maybe someday."

He believed in going now.

And he believed that if the mission was right, the path would reveal itself.

He chased what others only dreamed about... and turned what others thought impossible into reality.

That's why he built Turning Point USA in the first place.

That's why tens of thousands of students were inspired by Charlie to start chapters of their own -- _many in schools where they were explicitly told not to. _

**And that 's why today -- less than a year later -- we're not in 1,200 schools anymore: **

You’re not asleep! But yes, most people would dream of receiving an email like this one. I personally created the 47th President Founders Club for one reason only: To permanently honor the patriots who founded and carried the entire MAGA movement from Day One! The ones who never wavered, never surrendered, and refused to let them destroy our country twice. I had my team pull the very best files, millions of patriot names, and I went through them myself. Your name rose straight to the top. ** That’s why I’m personally inviting you to become a Charter Member of my 47th President Founders Club. Only a few spots exist in the entire country. I’m holding one for you! ** Don’t miss your shot to stand with the patriots who made the greatest comeback in American history. Your name could be one of them. I am counting on you especially at this very moment in time. body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1380%2E1086043%2EUYwp10)
Let me level with you, Peter.
**Tonight is a major filing deadline for our re-election campaign.** We’re required to report to the state of Maryland how much we’ve raised so far -- a major test of the strength of our team.
**[Will you pitch in $5 to our campaign before midnight? I wouldn’t ask if it weren’t important for the rest of our campaign.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260512-1.yKOOme&refcode=em-20260512-1&t=2&akid=1380%2E1086043%2EUYwp10)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260512-1.yKOOme&amount=5&refcode=em-20260512-1&t=21&akid=1380%2E1086043%2EUYwp10)**
Our opponents are keeping an eye on what we’re able to accomplish before this deadline, Peter. They’re afraid of the results we’ve delivered for Maryland. From public safety improvements to funding public education, Republicans are trying to roll it all back.
They know that we’re at a big disadvantage coming off being unable to fundraise for three months. But here’s what I know, Peter: **This team does not back down from a fight. If they want to tear down our accomplishments, let them try.**
**[If you want to defend this seat, I’m asking you to chip in $10 or $25 right now. Every dollar we raise now will help us fight whatever Republicans throw at us in the months to come.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260512-1.yKOOme&refcode=em-20260512-1&t=22&akid=1380%2E1086043%2EUYwp10)**
Thank you for being part of this team.
Elevate,
Wes

---|---|---
HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has personally confirmed to me that HHS referred Dutch-born NIH virologist Vincent Munster to the FBI after explosive whistleblower allegations accused him, and several foreign-born colleagues, of illegally smuggling dangerous virus samples from Africa into the United States.
Sec. Kennedy confirmed the referral in response to my reporting on a whistleblower letter first exposed by [White Coat Waste](https://substack.com/redirect/4c5ff455-c622-4795-b79e-7433174cb1b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which alleges a disturbing cover-up inside the NIH's taxpayer-funded Rocky Mountain Laboratories in Montana.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b9b9106a-1b4a-4b1b-b4e5-1c75bc506d2a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
> "We sent the referral to the FBI immediately," Kennedy told me. He added, "I assume he is going to prison."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/46d0352f-a5dc-4357-af6b-a17a09d87178?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2c03423c-fdc6-4ef3-b93f-f93d72fd405d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
That is a major admission from the sitting HHS Secretary. HHS has declined to comment to other reporters because this is an active FBI investigation, but my independent reporting on Kennedy's confirmation blows this story wide open.
Anthony Bellotti, President and Founder at government watchdog White Coat Waste, released the following [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/4c5ff455-c622-4795-b79e-7433174cb1b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on my findings:
> "White Coat Waste, founded in 2011, was the first to uncover, document, and expose Dr. Fauci's funding for gain-of-function animal experiments in Wuhan that almost certainly caused a lab leak and COVID--and we've warned that Vincent Munster's Fauci-backed animal tests with deadly bioagents at NIH's Rocky Mountain Lab (A.K.A. "Wuhan West") were another disaster waiting to happen on U.S. soil.
> Now, explosive new whistleblower claims exclusively obtained by White Coat Waste--alleging NIH cover-ups about Munster's reported virus smuggling and a monkey bite at RML, two stories we first scooped--have now been confirmed by HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. to Laura Loomer, further validating what we've been saying: Fauci-era taxpayer-funded animal labs are a grave threat and must be stopped.
> Our investigations and lawsuits have previously exposed Munster's maximum-pain animal tests with Ebola, his bat experiments with Chinese coronaviruses prior to the pandemic, and his involvement in a new Fauci-funded bat virus lab in Colorado.
> Munster is a mad scientist who has deep ties to EcoHealth Alliance and was involved in early proposals to engineer COVID-like viruses at the Wuhan lab. For years, White Coat Waste has led the fight to defund Munster and his maximum-pain animal labs, and we're currently calling out their continued Fauci-era funding with our 'WTF RFK?' billboards near NIH's Montana lab. The solution is simple: Stop the money. Stop the madness!"
What is really going on inside Rocky Mountain Laboratories, also known as RML? The whistleblower letter alleges that senior NIH officials went into "full cover-up mode" after a dangerous monkey bite incident and an alleged international pathogen smuggling scandal involving NIH researchers.
Chief of the Virus Ecology Section at RML, Vincent Munster, was reportedly removed from the HHS staff directory and placed on administrative leave following allegations that he and a colleague brought undeclared pathogen samples into the United States from the Democratic Republic of Congo without proper permits or documentation. This area is the origin of some of the deadliest diseases known to man like the Ebola virus.
The smuggled materials allegedly included samples tied to viral hemorrhagic fevers and monkeypox. According to the whistleblower letter [sent](https://substack.com/redirect/4c5ff455-c622-4795-b79e-7433174cb1b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to White Coat Waste:
_" Three foreign nationals with TDS who hate America and worked to weaponize the Covid virus got caught trying to sneak VHF samples into the United States from Africa."_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b5de7f24-8915-4d9d-b8ce-f9f6563945bb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
VHF stands for viral hemorrhagic fever, and it includes some of the most dangerous pathogens in the world. Taxpayers have every right to know why anyone connected to a federal lab would allegedly attempt to bring undeclared pathogen samples into the country.
The whistleblower letter includes several other disturbing details that align with previously reported concerns about RML. The whistleblower alleges:
_" Animal handler [name redacted] was bitten by an infected monkey (macaque) that was being tortured (infected and sickened with no pain mitigation) as an experiment for Crimean Congo Hemorrhagic fever."_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4f586f99-b84d-4c74-9e15-eeade5bc091c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
White Coat Waste previously exposed a lab accident involving the same virus at the same NIH lab, making this part of a disturbing pattern. In January, White Coat Waste reported that documents showed RML had quietly reported a deadly "select agent" was "released, lost, or stolen" in November 2025.
The monkey bite detail had not previously been public. If true, and Kennedy didn't deny any of the claims made in the whistleblower letter, this is a massive taxpayer-funded biosecurity scandal.
According to the whistleblower, senior NIH officials allegedly failed to properly alert the broader RML campus community about the risks after the monkey bite incident. The letter further alleges that decisions made by senior officials at NIH headquarters under NIH Director Dr. Jay Bhattacharya have protected legacy programs and entrenched bureaucrats rather than fully exposing what happened. The whistleblower claims:
_" Decisions made by the deep state, Fauci acolytes seem designed to prevent any attempts at accountability and to thwart the new administration's attempts to reign in the NIH bureaucratic kingdoms that have developed and thrived under the Fauci system of bioweapons research."_
For years, Americans were told to blindly trust the same federal health bureaucracy that funded risky research, hid behind redactions, smeared critics, cried "trust the science," defended animal abuse in government labs, and demanded endless taxpayer funding with almost no accountability.
Now, another whistleblower is alleging that dangerous pathogens, foreign researchers, and animal experiments were mishandled inside RML. We deserve answers.
Munster's research background includes work on virus ecology, zoonotic transmission, and bat coronavirus studies, all of which have become major flashpoints in the national debate over gain-of-function research, pandemic origins, biosafety failures, and the role of foreign-linked researchers inside America's federal science agencies. His name and active email address still appear on the NIH website despite Kennedy's admission to me that Munster is under FBI investigation and will likely go to prison.
White Coat Waste and I have been warning the public and the White House for over a year about anti-Trump and pro-Fauci holdovers still embedded inside HHS and NIH. Bureaucrats at these agencies are still funding Fauci's horrible beagle tests, protecting dangerous animal labs, and defending the same system that helped create the COVID-era nightmare of government lies, mandates, and scientific corruption.
Fauci's replacement, Jeffrey Taubenberger, a senior NIH virology official and gain-of-function researcher, now oversees the NIH animal lab involved in these incidents that are now allegedly being covered up.
HHS is allowing the same bureaucracy that created the crisis to police itself. That's a recipe for disaster and zero accountability. The public cannot rely on federal health bureaucrats to investigate other federal health bureaucrats, especially when the same agencies have spent years defending the research networks and flawed institutional culture that is now under immense public scrutiny.
The alleged monkey bite incident involving Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever was just the tip of the iceberg. Earlier reporting had already raised concerns about a lab accident involving the same virus at RML, but the whistleblower's allegation that a macaque bite occurred during these experiments is being reported here for the first time.
Without whistleblowers, the public would never know what is happening inside these taxpayer-funded labs. Without outside dedicated watchdogs like White Coat Waste, the NIH would keep hiding behind bureaucratic obscurity, redactions, and "no comment" statements while Americans are forced to fund dangerous virus experiments and abusive animal testing at their own expense.
No criminal charges have been publicly announced at this time, and the FBI investigation remains active. NIH and HHS have not issued a detailed public explanation beyond the reported administrative actions and Kennedy's confirmation that the matter was referred to federal law enforcement.
Taxpayers are once again being asked to trust a federal health bureaucracy that has repeatedly demanded secrecy while spending public money on dangerous and morally indefensible "research" that is ultimately just animal abuse conducted by mad scientists in white lab coats.
This is why the Trump administration must immediately accelerate reforms at NIH. That means stricter oversight of foreign researchers, immediate transparency on biosafety incidents, tougher import controls for pathogen samples, a full public audit of animal testing programs, and the removal of every Fauci, Obama, and Biden-era holdover who protects the flawed system instead of protecting the American people.
The NIH's abusive animal labs must be shut down before another lab accident, cover-up, or global health disaster is unleashed on the public.
NIH does not need another internal review designed to protect the institution. It needs accountability, transparency, and a full public reckoning.

body:
They've been running phony commercials. It's time to set them straight. |
Peter - If you live in Texas, you might have seen some of the phony ads my establishment opponent has been running.

**New state-by-state projections are showing Donald Trump’s approval down about 19 points here in Texas.**
This is huge news for this race because Greg Abbott has chosen, time after time, to tie himself to Trump.
Trump has endorsed Abbott three times. And when Trump called to redraw maps to favor Republicans, Abbott rushed to redraw our congressional maps to help hang onto power.

Because we’re all tired of Abbott. We’re tired of the corruption. Tired of the chaos. Tired of watching our schools, healthcare, and basic affordability lose priority while he plays political games just to stay in power.
That is the opening we have right now — and we’re already seeing voters reject the GOP at the ballot box in recent local elections.

Peter,

It's Gary Sinise here. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 _ _ and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. I've served as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. nearly every year since American Veterans Center revived it in 2005. **But I've never been more excited to serve as an Honorary Grand Marshall than I am this year - the year of America's 250****th**** birthday.**

Peter, this Memorial Day marks the first major national act of remembrance of the veterans who made the ultimate sacrifice to defend America from its enemies and ensure it has remained the Land of the Free for the last 250 years. And this year's National Memorial Day Parade will be a special edition - the biggest parade yet - where national memory meets living history as veterans from every military generation celebrate America and honor the service and sacrifice of their fallen brethren. **Peter, the National Memorial Day Parade is ENIRELY FUNDED by private contributions, including from generous patriots like you.** **[In light of America’s 250th birthday and the special opportunity we have to honor veterans this year, will you chip in today to help support the parade with a gift of $25, $50, $75, $150, or more?](http://links.standingstrongamerica.com/u/click?_t=29c3b6e742c849fabbcc130432510e66&_m=76b98b14e38a4d8ebe6c1a05a7115c41&_e=_EteRjD0Zdc8KbFEX5omAA5U6v9uJhVTKfKKUtDXP-YNMXnQgAZ6EsNt3fBE7sULTSSdy3cUuLPdv_9ixATiR7KfxqhAeVfWG_itTX3flTl7Bv8R4A2CId-VbKKwwI4b_qXGyLKpiWaCGjo0-7SdPCFKQgNcTeFyygVz5QfZNvxvqPiIDGwBJX6xJQRBzHvqwtSkdOYGSRvjxwNC2e_LZMS9alvFLaQ54_lgpohsxHj5Fx6G02R_Um_s7B84DnWeycMZtZ_g-BHmyZFp_XPULl4MF4erTosh6INoU2mLgYAHSO0clzh4Hcv_CQlIRHAS1CjCVEhyGji0Xa7b5jDK4FXVHo9gsRpfUFGB3W9nAy7sDg5VxXWF_gZDpk-aa2Oq6z91nGAITutkcQeO_0V17bCKmXxW1TpXUJcycq21nEIMys_lRlXfZfPW7UpXQM1qjCXvB0Loi5gSqutxXOoBgW9L_QJiHrScGzq1KOA48LXtLYCv-tyj9r-V4EW5fKiUIZmPH85rH9wNt18KhFS6jTEqyDTSCsK8hUleJ5cVMGYuimgbcUbGO7pm0oe8q9tnvqDA5RukFEKLXracd07kiLN9UxfnX4_medOeLKKzbsgikI3XPu5Da6dmB9REY__y3e_saaEwh5Hpusp040u_Ul7BARnnmtR5YKHX9Dg5GZpVNzwJEEh5RaNQG3lou_REg-z1YKcZIqkmimRrdkqSiA%3D%3D)**

clean_body: Honor our veterans with me| | | | Peter, It's Gary Sinise here. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. I've served as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. nearly every year since American Veterans Center revived it in 2005. But I've never been more excited to serve as an Honorary Grand Marshall than I am this year - the year of America's 250th birthday. Peter, this Memorial Day marks the first major national act of remembrance of the veterans who made the ultimate sacrifice to defend America from its enemies and ensure it has remained the Land of the Free for the last 250 years. And this year's National Memorial Day Parade will be a special edition - the biggest parade yet - where national memory meets living history as veterans from every military generation celebrate America and honor the service and sacrifice of their fallen brethren. Peter, the National Memorial Day Parade is ENIRELY FUNDED by private contributions, including from generous patriots like you. WWII veterans were a key part of the first parade when it was revived in 2005, as they have been every year since for the last 20 years. But this may be the last year we have the opportunity to have these brave men and women with us for the parade. | | | | | | | | This year is a rare moment when living witnesses to World War II and America 's 250th birthday overlap. And no matter how much you can give to this important cause, I want to ask something additional of you. On Memorial Day - not just this momentous year of military milestones, but every year - please join me in honoring those who made the ultimate sacrifice for our freedoms. Come to the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. Visit a local veterans' cemetery. Send a note to a family of the fallen. Or simply take a quiet moment to think about the men and women who gave their lives to defend OUR country. I believe that while we can never do enough to express our gratitude to our defenders, veterans, and first responders, we can always do a little more. FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASEMay 12, 2026katherine@julialetlow.com
**Monroe Mayor Friday Ellis Endorses Congresswoman Julia Letlow for U.S. Senate** _Ellis highlights Letlow’s Northeast Louisiana roots and record of delivering for the region_
**BATON ROUGE, LA** — Today, Congresswoman Julia Letlow, the Trump-endorsed conservative candidate for the U.S. Senate in Louisiana, announced the endorsement of Monroe Mayor Friday Ellis.
Mayor Ellis praised Letlow’s deep roots in Northeast Louisiana and her commitment to fighting for the people of the region.
_“I’ve always been proud to say I’m from here, and so is Julia Letlow,”_ **said Mayor Friday Ellis.**_“She knows Northeast Louisiana because her roots are right here in this dirt. We don't have time for Washington politicians who just want to hear themselves talk. We need fighters who actually deliver, and Julia delivers.”_
_“We’re in the middle of an economic revival in Monroe, building a community where our kids can actually stay to live, work, and raise families of their own. But to keep that momentum, we need to keep our people in the fight._
_“I need you to lock arms with your neighbors, get to the polls this Saturday, and send Julia Letlow back to Washington to keep kicking down doors for Northeast Louisiana.”_
_“I’m incredibly grateful to have Mayor Ellis’ support,”_**said Congresswoman Letlow.**_“Friday understands what makes Northeast Louisiana special because, like me, he has lived it and fought for it. We both believe in creating opportunities so our children and grandchildren can build their future right here in Louisiana. I’m proud to stand alongside him as we continue fighting for our communities and delivering real results for the people of this state.”_
Letlow, a Monroe native, has represented Louisiana’s Fifth Congressional District since 2021 and currently serves on the House Appropriations Committee and House Education and the Workforce Committee. She is running for the U.S. Senate as the Trump-endorsed conservative in the race and has built her campaign around fighting for Louisiana families, securing the border, protecting parents’ rights, unleashing American energy, and delivering results for communities across the state.

CORRECTION
Door Knocking
TOMORROW, May 13th, 5 PM - 7 PM
The time was incorrectly listed as 10 AM - 12 PM on the last email.
Help knock doors around Gaithersburg! We'll be heading out to engage with voters, share the positive work happening in our district, and get people excited to re-elect Congresswoman April McClain Delaney.
Whether you have canvassed 1000 times or 0 times, this is a great chance to get involved with the campaign! We will begin with a quick training session before heading out, and go out in pairs; no experience is necessary!
Bring comfortable shoes, water, and whatever attire the weather dictates! It'll be a great day of conversation and community as we work towards re-electing Congresswoman Delaney. We can't wait to see you there!
Sign Up [https://www.mobilize.us/dashboard/aprilmcclaindelaneyforcongress/timeslot/5985971/]
(Virtual) Phone Banks
Thursday Night Phone Banks Sign Up [https://www.mobilize.us/aprilmcclaindelaneyforcongress/event/934939/]
Every Thursday night, 6-8 PM , until Election Night, we will have a virtual and in-person phone bank to turn out supporters and recruit more volunteers!
Either come on into the office or join from the comfort of your own home .
All you need is a phone and the willingness to make some calls. Hope to see you there!
Tuesday Night Phone Banks Sign Up [https://www.mobilize.us/aprilmcclaindelaneyforcongress/event/936896/]
Every Tuesday night, 6-8 PM, until Election Night, we will have a virtual phone bank, with an in-person option in Frederick coming soon. Help turn out supporters and grow our volunteer base!
Join from the comfort of your own home.
Gaithersburg Office Volunteering
Tuesday - Friday, 10 AM - 6 PM, Every Week
Join us at the campaign office to help re-elect Congresswoman April McClain Delaney! Our office is open Tuesday - Friday from 10 AM to 6 PM, and volunteers can jump in however they’d like—whether that’s knocking doors, making phone calls, or helping with important office projects that keep the campaign running.
You’re welcome to pop in for an hour or stay longer, whatever fits your schedule. We just ask that you sign up ahead of time so we can make sure we have materials, lists, and snacks ready for you. It’s a great way to meet fellow supporters, build community, and make a real impact in the campaign .
Sign Up Here [https://www.mobilize.us/aprilmcclaindelaneyforcongress/event/942348/]

body:
A Rodney King-era civil rights law drives the federal lawsuit over Colorado’s magazine ban
| | | | [](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/s2paa1d45bf)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/sbofbf222a0)**
| | Hi friends!
Another round of speakers is dropping today for Freedom Festival but you MUST be on the [Priority List](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/s1j3ea730f1) to be the first to know! Sign up here.
Want your full news breakdown? Listen to the Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/s9ua683beb8), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/s4t1cbefcd6) or [Rumble](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/scmcaf8f15d). Here's a summary of today's top stories:
**🏛️ Under the Golden Dome...** Gov. Jared Polis is weighing a [bill allowing lawsuits against federal immigration agents](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/sah4dc72560), while Senate Democrats advanced a plan [redirecting roughly $306 million in future TABOR refunds](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/s3s3b0b1e15) despite expected legal challenges. Debate over crime policy continues as critics warn sentencing reforms have [weakened public safety,](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/scs23dab2b5) while lawmakers also face scrutiny over [transportation “workarounds”](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/sdpdcf9aa4e) and insurance fees critics say are [quietly raising homeowner costs](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/s4qfcbdb0bc).
**🏔️ Here in Colorado...** Jeffco Schools Superintendent Tracy Dorland resigned after five years leading the state’s second-largest district following a [teachers union “no confidence” vote](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/s2j7c450234). Meanwhile, new surveillance footage intensified concerns over airport security after a [trespasser reached an active DIA runway](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/s3h70d2ca06) and was struck by a departing Frontier flight carrying 231 passengers. Colorado’s gun laws are also under renewed federal scrutiny as the Trump administration’s DOJ challenges the state’s 15-round magazine ban, arguing it [violates Second Amendment protections](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/sbtb4adb2af).
**🇺🇸 On the National Stage...** The Trump administration’s DOJ is moving to revoke citizenship from 12 individuals accused of [concealing criminal or terrorism-related backgrounds](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/seo20080a8a) during naturalization, including allegations tied to child sexual assault, al Qaeda activity, and terrorism financing. Meanwhile, federal reports show [improper government payments reached nearly $186 billion](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/scv8e152342) in fiscal year 2025, fueling concerns about weak oversight, fraud vulnerabilities, and billions in taxpayer dollars lost through government programs.
This is your Mountain Minute for Tuesday, May 12, 2026.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[A Rodney King-era civil rights law drives the federal lawsuit over Colorado’s magazine ban](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/s5qa803caf5)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/s0k3a01f7ca)
[](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/s2rc7268d06)
Colorado’s magazine ban has been challenged before. The surprise this time is not the Second Amendment argument. It is the DOJ’s decision to use a federal civil-rights law traditionally aimed at police misconduct investigations to make it. On May 5, federal attorneys filed against Denver over its assault-weapons ban. The next morning, they were back in court with another complaint—this one against the state, over the 15-round magazine limit.
The law driving both lawsuits came out of the aftermath of Rodney King. Congress passed §12601 in 1994 after Los Angeles erupted in riots, giving the federal government authority to intervene when police departments repeatedly violated constitutional rights. DOJ has used the law fewer than 100 times in the three decades since.
Until this year, never to enforce the Second Amendment. The lawsuits mark a significant expansion in how DOJ is using federal civil-rights authority.

**[When the people vote, the majority should not pre-load a workaround](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/s4gfde71ae6)** BY C. J. GARBO, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/s0v0f395719)
* **Commentary warns lawmakers are preparing a “workaround” to voter decisions:** The piece argues HB26-1430 was designed as a conditional response to Initiative 175, allowing lawmakers to blunt the impact of a transportation funding measure before voters have even cast ballots.
* **Critics say the bill reflects growing disregard for voter intent:** Supporters describe the measure as protecting funding for priorities like schools and healthcare, while the commentary argues it treats voters’ decisions as a threat to be managed rather than respected.
* **Debate framed as larger fight over government accountability:** The article says the issue extends beyond transportation policy, warning that increasing use of fiscal “offsets” and procedural maneuvers risks weakening public trust and insulating political insiders from voter-driven change.

**[Polis Faces Decision On Bill Allowing Lawsuits Against Immigration Agents](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/s0rf3390441)** [THE COLORADO SUN](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/s9g8dcd5343)
* **Colorado lawmakers pass bill allowing lawsuits against ICE agents:** Senate Bill 5 would let Coloradans sue federal immigration officers in state court over alleged constitutional violations during enforcement operations, and now heads to Gov. Jared Polis for consideration.
* **Measure advances amid Trump immigration crackdown:** Supporters say the bill creates accountability for federal agents, while critics argue it targets immigration enforcement as arrests have increased under the Trump administration’s tougher border and deportation policies.
* **Legal and constitutional questions continue to grow:** Similar laws in other states have already faced court challenges over federal authority, and opponents warn the Colorado measure could trigger broader legal battles over states attempting to regulate federal immigration operations.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/s0qdc4a1b16)**
|

**[Manny Rutinel wants to represent Colorado’s oil country. His law is bearing down on its only refinery.](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/sdhf67a845e)**
**[](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/s7t28ed8cbc)****BY JEN SCHUMANN | STATE | MAY 8** _State Rep. Manny Rutinel is asking voters in the heart of Colorado’s oil country to send him to Congress. Seven weeks from now, a law Rutinel helped write could reshape how Colorado’s only petroleum refinery operates._
__
**[As EEOC complaints climb, former federal official teaches Colorado workers their rights](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/sbu2cc293be)**
**[](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/s3neffdc771)****BY JEN SCHUMANN | STATE | MAY 7** _A congressional candidate is teaching workplace discrimination law to the public as Congress faces new harassment scrutiny and the EEOC operates with its smallest workforce in nearly half a century._
__

**[Big business taxes, small family credits, and a permanent tax on overtime](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/s4nff01fcad)**
**[](https://link.email.joinrmv.__g/sfpd540bf96)****BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | MAY 7** _Rep. Yara Zokaie stood before the House Finance Committee on March 9 and made the case for HB26-1221, a bill targeting executive pay deductions and corporate loss carry-forwards. “Our families are struggling to juggle their rent, groceries, and utilities,” she said. The legislature had a choice. It could “choose to protect tax breaks for millionaire CEO salaries” or “allow for a break for our hard-working Coloradan families.”_
__

| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131271665/620523068/326965909?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_Ballroom_260512_T1_2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3NjUyNjhmNC0zODRlLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=lWKkRTcmeeZDdAVQgZU-C3vIPlTuT_lxBg4QNdwitdY=) Derek, this is outrageous.

Virginians – and many Americans – are facing an affordability crisis of President Trump’s own making. Millions are losing access to health care. Home ownership feels out of reach for far too many young Americans. Gas prices are skyrocketing due to Trump’s war-of-choice. And his solution? President Trump wants taxpayers to spend **$1 BILLION** to pay for his White House ballroom.

**You read that right – $1 billion.**

And to put that in perspective, we did the math. _What would $1 billion buy Virginians instead?_

It could restore SNAP benefits for five years to the 100,913 Virginians who saw their benefits slashed by Trump and Congressional Republicans.

It could restore health care for 25% of the Virginia residents who will lose their Medicaid coverage due to Trump’s cuts.

It could cover child care for 59,437 infants.

It could cover a full year of rent for 46,399 Virginia households, or a year of electricity for 520,833 households, or it could build 2,000 brand new affordable homes.

**The bottom line is this: Trump is more concerned with White House vanity projects than actually making life better for working families facing an affordability crisis. “Get your cotton-picking hands off of Virginia.”
#
What do you do if you’re being interviewed by someone and, when referring to House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, they say: **“Get your cotton-picking hands off of Virginia.”**
If you are a normal person, you don’t tolerate it. You refuse to be a party to that comment because it is completely, totally, blatantly racist.
But if you are Congresswoman Jen Kiggans, you say: **"That's right. Ditto. Yes. Yes, to that."** No, seriously, that actually happened.
Kiggans represents Virginia’s Second Congressional District, a district with deep connections to the Navy and a large Veteran community. 780,000 people live in CD-2, and roughly 22% of them are black. Kiggans just showed each what she really thinks about them.
Comments like this are beneath the dignity of a Member of Congress. Period. Jen Kiggans needs to resign from the House immediately.

What we’re seeing right now is a five-alarm fire for American democracy.
FIRST: The Trump administration tried to coerce states across the country into turning over sensitive voter data — personal information belonging to millions of Americans.
THEN: Donald Trump signed an executive order attempting to ban mail-in voting — making it harder for working families, seniors, rural voters, and people with disabilities to participate in our democracy.
NOW: The Supreme Court has handed him another chilling victory by gutting the Voting Rights Act , opening the door to unchecked racial gerrymandering and allowing politicians to redraw maps to protect their hold on power.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
FIGHT BACK [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
This is not happening in isolation. It’s a coordinated, escalating effort to weaken the guardrails of our democracy — one rule, one court decision, one executive order at a time.
And here in Oregon, we know what’s at stake. Free and fair elections don’t survive on their own — they only survive if people are willing to defend them.
That’s why this work matters so much. As Secretary of State, I’ve fought to protect secure, accessible elections and ensure that every eligible Oregonian can cast a ballot and have it counted.
But the attacks are getting more aggressive, and the defenses need to get stronger. We need to be ready to push back —politically, legally, in the press, and at the ballot box — against anyone trying to rig the system in their favor.
That’s why I’m asking you to chip in $50, $25, or even $10 today. Your support powers this fight to protect voting rights, defend election workers, and make sure Oregon continues to be a national model for fair elections. Because democracy only works if we fight for it. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]

# We've been busy. Come find us this week.

Peter,Things are moving, and we just added a bunch of events this week. I want to make sure you know where to find us because I would love to see your face at one of these.
---
| [Upcoming Events](https://us.list-manage.com/18xOg7Jc60Z?e=0c0d11993f&c2id=6a676d78c90e8a1f5821c8d4ac39abd8)
---
| |
First up, tonight.**The St. Croix County Dems monthly meeting** is happening right here in my backyard at Champs Sports Bar and Grill in New Richmond at 6 pm. We will be collecting signatures for our nomination papers, and if you are lucky, you might even catch me singing a song with Paul. Come on out.**Thursday the 14th** is a day I am genuinely honored to be part of. We will be joining veterans, families, and community members at two separate tributes honoring the Hmong and Lao veterans of the Vietnam War on the 51st anniversary of the evacuation and refugee crisis. These are the hidden heroes of that war, and they deserve every bit of recognition we can give them. We will be at the Wisconsin Veterans Tribute in **Cadott from 10 am to 11:30 am** and then at**The Highground Veterans Memorial Park in Neillsville from 1 pm to 4 pm**.**On Friday the 15th,** we are heading to Wausau for a meet-and-greet at Tucknee Coffee Company from 1 pm to 3 pm.Come grab a cup, pull up a chair, tell me what is on your mind, and help us get some signatures on those nomination papers while you are at it. Music included.**Saturday the 16th** is a full day. We are starting with the **Vilas Dems Pancake Breakfast** in Woodruff from 8 am to noon because pancakes and politics are a combination I will never say no to. Then we are heading to Pioneer Park in Rhinelander for the **Defending Democracy Rally** with Northern Lights Indivisible from noon to 2 pm. We are wrapping up the evening at the Potawatomi Casino and Hotel in Wabeno for the **Tribal Nations Event** at 7 pm alongside Francesca Hong, Ginger Murray, and State Treasurer Yee Leng Xiong for a conversation about indigenous rights and priorities. A Livestream will be available if you cannot make it in person.If you cannot make it to any of these but want to help move things along,[ a donation to the campaign](https://us.list-manage.com/tZRwdZpKTZD?e=0c0d11993f&c2id=6a676d78c90e8a1f5821c8d4ac39abd8) goes further than you might think, and we are grateful for every single one.And if you haven't picked up a nomination paper yet,[ you can find it right here.](https://us.list-manage.com/q4WoYAwPohO?e=0c0d11993f&c2id=6a676d78c90e8a1f5821c8d4ac39abd8) We need signatures to get on the August ballot, and every one counts.See you out there.Thanks, Chris ~:|

name: Kristen McDonald Rivet
subject: I want to hear from you directly, friend.
body:
|
#
Friend, This first year in Congress has really reinforced something for me: people are just plain tired. Tired of the division. Tired of the political games. And tired of working hard while it feels like everything just keeps getting more expensive. My team and I have spent the last year all over mid-Michigan – in union halls, family farms, church basements, and living rooms – and no matter where we go, we hear the same thing: **People want leaders who will actually do something.** And look, Washington can be very frustrating. But I still believe bringing people together to get things done matters. It’s how we stopped Elon Musk from closing the Saginaw Social Security office. It’s how we protected funding for the Flint Registry when MAGA Republicans tried to cut it. And it’s how we passed my bipartisan hot rotisserie chicken bill out of the House, which is going to help SNAP families take home a hot, ready-to-go meal. That’s the work I came here to do: lower costs, take on corruption, protect health care, and fight for working families. But there’s still a lot more to do, and before this campaign really picks up, I want to hear from you. body:
The Democrats’ latest scheme is the most un-American slap in the face to the Constitution I have ever heard.

| Peter,
I thought we had already seen the worst of the Democrats' dirty tricks and blatant power grabs...
-> They flooded the airwaves with cash to spread lies about my record on TV.
-> They vandalized my campaign office and destroyed our signs.
-> They targeted me with endless dark money from Left-leaning Super PACs.
-> They even spent MILLIONS attempting to redraw our congressional maps and wipe out fair representation in the Commonwealth of Virginia.
But their latest scheme is the most un-American slap in the face to the Constitution I have ever heard:

ICYMI: The US Supreme Court just heard a case that every American family should know about.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_dhs_email-26q2?refcode=x_260512_roundup_act [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_dhs_email-26q2?refcode=x_260512_roundup_act]
A man named John Durnell used the weed killer Roundup for years. When it gave him cancer, he did what we tell people to do in this country: he went to court and sued.
Now Bayer, one of the most powerful corporations on Earth, is asking the Supreme Court to say it doesn’t matter.
They’re one of these Goliaths that try to use the law to control our lives. They’re not even arguing that Roundup didn't cause John’s cancer. They're arguing it’s not for a jury to decide—that they’re above the law.
This isn’t just about one man or one product. It’s part of a coordinated legal project by the biggest corporations in the world.
Big Tech giants are designing addictive algorithms that target our kids and making it harder to opt out. Big Ag giants are putting chemicals in our fields, and our bodies, and hiding what they know—just like Big Oil and Big Tobacco did for generations.
And they think they can get away with it. Federal preemption, forced arbitration, corporate immunity: those are all just fancy legal terms for one simple idea.
Mega-corporations want to rig the system, decide what’s safe for your family, and make sure you can’t hold them accountable when they’re wrong.
One of the most important functions of government is keeping people safe.
I’m running for Attorney General of Colorado because we still have the tools to fight back: strong consumer protection laws, competition laws, and the power to take corporations to court. I will use every single one of them.
If we’re going to win this race and protect Colorado families, we need the resources to take them on head-on.
