The results are real. | | | [](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=2431179778b34901a4904f895fc40039&_e=KfS3GOPG9i-nSul99KGl8vg5zFmjRwY0B0qN-DO7ctvaKl8UvKzTZSY4aKTUtiHUjYCkUjwVm0CsMOeI1J5NUQAjZlg_aO4LJviVfx0gF7XZxeMWzJYJyDCa_k6AuAx3T_HVSQdSoivjKpuBE8AHh9RUry5q6Ix-etO2v4jIxwo4i9R52CMPkB0CNLoC0ZWj4WDWmSiR0sj8BSNzbHryleKqbWm1SSF0xislVmdwEXmG7xCBOx1UG8EJXEapcnlUdT1lEf-P2BAu5NUinGSMjzHhce28F4L6hKN_zGIzNS9evQNdZeAP5_LFWL_vTShyUBlU7GSd-BajKEMpQcfgD067d7RK0t0ezRZsvMCCrsO-1cNTSo8rheH1A4swoQ5S2Yvf51Uee8e1EyD3ErxkFesGeIi3DMf7bkX49cpHav93i6LLhyQ8h27rU13bqZodAyGTAbabSb8y4myacHD3DCRAcCiDLS7N3vtOTlaQrkCloFyr7tvoBlTkNTQhnEGYytmKVHW2aW4AqUWf0rO3Mr0AgEJM5BmMRis3RgOwqpNEDR1nl8sIYVrhCri_C61lviabJG5mgqXygBWJilmoidYfCoiFebhLf1398GnCeXVDHJUQPerDMK8HZTYkNfUFeqF_h9RD-iYG_jh95Y-kOqB9GdhZH_86ioOs3VgOx7Q6vHFEqQjr8qavXJDjHeEwBco0v-CSa8fWsBWcTWRLgA%3D%3D)
---
| | Peter,
---
If you ever doubted we could win America's youth back from the Left...

If you ever wondered whether we'd lost the next generation for good...

If you ever sat up at night -- watching the news, seeing what's happening in our schools, our culture, our country -- and thought, _" Is it already too late?" _

You're not alone.

A lot of good people have been asking the same question.

**But I want to tell you something that might just change how you feel about the future of this country... **

Just one year ago, Turning Point USA's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools.

That was no small feat.

Starting a single chapter today takes serious courage. Students get mocked. Threatened. Investigated. Sometimes even physically attacked.

So reaching 1,200 chapters already felt like a miracle.

_Then Charlie called me... _

He said: "Andrew, I love what we're doing with our high school program -- but we've got to move faster."

I told him, "We are."

Charlie replied, "No you're not thinking what I'm thinking... I want to be in 35,000 high schools."

I laughed. I told him, "Charlie, there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America."

"Okay," he said, "How many are there?"

"About 27,000."

Without skipping a beat, Charlie said, "Okay, great. Let's do 27,000!"
I'll be honest -- I froze.

We didn't have the numbers. We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the roadmap yet.

But he wasn't fazed.

He said, "Don't worry. We'll figure it out. We'll do it together."

That was Charlie.

He didn't think small. He didn't move slow. He didn't settle for "maybe someday."

He believed in going now.

And he believed that if the mission was right, the path would reveal itself.

He chased what others only dreamed about... and turned what others thought impossible into reality.

That's why he built Turning Point USA in the first place.

That's why tens of thousands of students were inspired by Charlie to start chapters of their own -- _many in schools where they were explicitly told not to. _

**And that 's why today -- less than a year later -- we're not in 1,200 schools anymore: **
---
[](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=2431179778b34901a4904f895fc40039&_e=KfS3GOPG9i-nSul99KGl8vg5zFmjRwY0B0qN-DO7ctvaKl8UvKzTZSY4aKTUtiHUjYCkUjwVm0CsMOeI1J5NUQAjZlg_aO4LJviVfx0gF7XZxeMWzJYJyDCa_k6AuAx3T_HVSQdSoivjKpuBE8AHh9RUry5q6Ix-etO2v4jIxwo4i9R52CMPkB0CNLoC0ZWj4WDWmSiR0sj8BSNzbHryleKqbWm1SSF0xislVmdwEXmG7xCBOx1UG8EJXEapcnlUIt3VtENXrEb56SlEoakHD--qvtBODPBezBCZ5zvgRHK_S3_xiYYcLQSjqWw88vabhDpgGmqLlLk5cgKTmTNUwUVxo3O5W5qpEk0UB-on0q8PriXewXi2mlKD-nBRskyjomua821zLZKe6typ3WEzTQ0uFpoN4MmhS-8W8EhIKrtZ9o0gVbRHsQ0PeBvoqtPIy0kHW_33Lnkd8Vx15XNiuyHVl7Eg-59VIVtZr1V5A9BbJ313n01GTD4fXoGQuHAA9EkBsFH4cwdOpe3JGkyFFTCn3MZbo_WIk3gG073Qkr5Y82TTVUxSrwDtONO8SOt6fiyN_DhiYql9hg76N5c5j4ZD23uW8SfmFG4nFX4ABUltI2qP6hNaJwwBA_o3GZ42B7kcvbK6izCdQlfKQtP4g4dq76n-24Y3whiUWXOjAtMMM8EK3V5SaTC88xVjvuxuH_U9CP1w6gSCjuGdUPcaXQ%3D%3D)
---
We're in 3,300.

That's roughly 13% of all high schools in America.

Eight states have officially partnered with Club America to bring our chapters into every school statewide.

✅ Florida
✅ Texas
✅ Tennessee
✅ Oklahoma
✅ Montana
✅ Nebraska
✅ Arkansas
✅ Indiana

And we're just getting started.

Think about that: 13% of America's youth now have a place at school where they can say it's okay to love this country...

That it's okay to be bold. That it's okay to believe in God, in family, and in freedom.

_That 's what Club America is about... _

**Giving the next generation a place where they can find their courage, develop grit, and learn how to lead the fight for their country. **
---
[](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=2431179778b34901a4904f895fc40039&_e=KfS3GOPG9i-nSul99KGl8vg5zFmjRwY0B0qN-DO7ctvaKl8UvKzTZSY4aKTUtiHUjYCkUjwVm0CsMOeI1J5NUQAjZlg_aO4LJviVfx0gF7XZxeMWzJYJyDCa_k6AuAx3T_HVSQdSoivjKpuBE8AHh9RUry5q6Ix-etO2v4jIxwo4i9R52CMPkB0CNLoC0ZWj4WDWmSiR0sj8BSNzbHryleKqbWm1SSF0xislVmdwEXmG7xCBOx1UG8EJXEapcnlU_FW1HqPZZFNn8I_qZDIvJ3DVvCvo1JvhycpxvpVI8EASIB4xUTpdBKR6PyX5aaRwIk3LNgxZyGRgA3TqXhE1AcTyZVM9Z7ks5aDtfa-5M_IDowJPyrWgqQTZeX-Y9qNBfRoAH0nYH7Asu2dy9zYIQW5Ysby6bfCA6nlBZf2yDtD7T_2fJ3XnFcAqpb-DLhy17SxlaApgdv9daLH2DD2IPHRlr2aOOYqP_9WfcgwLjRZ64kjjn_lpiLaqFokFdaAE6hw2I3iJwIhz5qxaTgbn0mX3BA08lHqEYqentaN7hQFjw9tNshYHlrAteflw4JMQLJ5MtM4mobf7GnB-aZewALW7JoKYapJMqUViY-gyjeDd-g3mB5R8Z2w_LswpMo9jOkcPTpXnbxNpnk5DBUCDZj6GnRD48xNvbWvkJqyQ2aHiL3HgQAjHKiE_Du7vJfkLXMgXQ5cW5S9MdgfNHYq7-Q%3D%3D)
---
_But now, Peter, the question is... _

**What will it take to bring Club America to the next 3,300 schools? What will it take to bring it to all 27,000? **

Because here's the truth:

These students aren't just signing up. _They 're stepping up. _

They're leading chapters in schools where America is attacked... where they're often targeted for daring to say what they believe... and where speaking the truth is dangerous.

But that isn't stopping them.

They're still showing up. They're speaking out. And they're growing stronger than ever.

They're becoming exactly the kind of young patriots Charlie believed in -- not just bold, _but brave_. Not just loud, but _principled_.

**Every time a student starts a new chapter, we make sure they 're not standing alone. **

**We send them an activism kit -- American flags, pocket Constitutions, chapter materials, and leadership tools. **

These kits give student leaders everything they need to rally their peers and stand strong on their campuses.

Each one costs just $25 to pack and ship.

**[If you’re able to, I hope you’ll help send a kit to the next student who raises their hand to lead by making your gift to Turning Point USA today.](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=2431179778b34901a4904f895fc40039&_e=KfS3GOPG9i-nSul99KGl8vg5zFmjRwY0B0qN-DO7ctvaKl8UvKzTZSY4aKTUtiHUjYCkUjwVm0CsMOeI1J5NUQAjZlg_aO4LJviVfx0gF7XZxeMWzJYJyDCa_k6AuAx3T_HVSQdSoivjKpuBE8AHh9RUry5q6Ix-etO2v4jIxwo4i9R52CMPkB0CNLoC0ZWj4WDWmSiR0sj8BSNzbHryleKqbWm1SSF0xislVmdwEXmG7xCBOx1UG8EJXEapcnlUSKp9bZi5QNieqt2y99BKDfoM5VZlaiHugCUWze7jevNyHPFp4u71NbIQgvXpnJjlTH3OzpZxXDSI-yRt0Pfr4WN8GaLd4xGwp7OBwE1bJKLkgACedwDNzml1Q3Ikwse9zZt_Tl7F6yTHjYbI74JfgOWAI87E_g5czh_b5M0qXsPxt2SOYtP9uFvhgFCDLmMYv6x1t02m0k9bjU7wLid8hhrAJa6e0vT6ud1jCy0PWeUFh2XW7nutX_mV-RXat_ig39pMeMJiM2YcT3ud19VDbuSjiKCI3pBNk4Jv4NoqHQUcxGMnHCoDeGYgProngRhKHogXrPXM-J_I-C-uOII0N4Tbiv3FBe76LjIoX6vf8LqWHFLXoo-vVS2fOul2CDQCWX30mrf5D2AXps_lVU2d3VoVY3e5V9e-8zgZCx-r_fmcswcAQkxWd839az4YriCgIDTBeM3k7QFm9O3SXHeysA%3D%3D)**

Today, I'm proud to join forces with Stand in the Gap, a non-profit organization dedicated to supporting the patriots who exercised their First Amendment rights in protest of the outcome of that election. I want to reach as many people as I can with this request... I told their founder, Shane Jenkins, that I would help him raise $20,000 before the end of the month to help Stand in the Gap provide help, hope, and healing to the January 6th patriots. Even a donation of $10 can give a January 6th patriot the support they need. Otherwise, let me explain why I 'm asking you to donate at least $10: $10 because the " crime" these patriots committed was fighting for their country. $10 because even though they've been pardoned, many of them are struggling to get back on their feet. $10 because Stand in the Gap is providing them with the resources they need to successfully reintegrate into their communities, find work, reconnect with family, and restore their rights. Not only are these men and women patriots, but they come from all walks of life -- law enforcement, veterans, white-collar professionals, blue-collar workers, and all races and religions. And they were hunted down in a political persecution that denied them their constitutional rights. Stand in the Gap exists to provide real, practical help, like rent money, job training, transportation, legal referrals, trauma counseling, and health insurance, to help these persecuted patriots move on with their lives. Your gift today can help one of these patriots find the help, hope, and healing they need to succeed in their second chance. Fellow Conservative,

My name is Adam Schwarze, and I'm a former Navy SEAL, Marine Corps veteran, and proud Minnesotan **running for U.S. Senate against Tim Walz's handpicked lieutenant governor—a politician even more radical than her boss.** I'm requesting your support in this critical battle to restore common-sense conservative values to Minnesota.

| | |

---](https://us.list-manage.com/g19t_F20OHa?e=95355a072c&c2id=cd64ea42b1b0eeac0fd7d107db75288a)
| | | | | | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
** May 12, 2026katherine@julialetlow.com
**FLEMING’S PERSONAL FORTUNE SURGED WHILE SERVING IN CONGRESS
** _Fleming’s reported net worth jumped from roughly $8 million to $35 million in one year_
**BATON ROUGE, LA** — John Fleming has spent this campaign trying to sell himself as a conservative outsider, but his record tells a very different story.
While serving in Congress, Fleming’s reported net worth surged from approximately $8 million to $35 million in one year, raising serious questions about how Fleming dramatically increased his personal fortune while holding federal office.
---
|
---
| | | | | | _Source:_[_OpenSecrets_](https://us.list-manage.com/lPGVshiw2rC?e=95355a072c&c2id=cd64ea42b1b0eeac0fd7d107db75288a) While Louisiana families were working harder to make ends meet, John Fleming was watching his reported net worth explode by tens of millions of dollars in Washington. Now, the same politician who got rich while serving in Congress is collecting a taxpayer-funded salary as State Treasurer while remaining on the payroll of a D.C. lobbying firm.That is exactly the kind of out-of-touch, self-serving political record voters are sick of.“John Fleming owes Louisiana voters a full explanation,” said Letlow Communications Director Katherine Thordahl. “His reported net worth exploded while he was in Congress, he later joined a D.C. lobbying firm, and now he has admitted that he remains a paid employee of that firm while serving as Louisiana State Treasurer. That is not the record of a conservative outsider. That is the record of a career politician who knows exactly how to work the system.”Fleming’s out-of-touch record goes back years. In a 2011 MSNBC interview, Fleming claimed his businesses brought in $6.3 million, but said his net income was “more like $600,000,” and that after he fed his family, he had “maybe $400,000 left over.” Fleming should immediately answer:How did his reported net worth increase from roughly $8 million to $35 million in one year while he was serving in Congress?What assets, transactions, investments, or business interests drove that increase?Did any of that wealth growth involve industries, companies, or business interests affected by federal policy?Did Fleming really spend $200,000 a year to feed his family? Why did Fleming join The McKeon Group after leaving federal office?Why is Fleming still a paid employee of The McKeon Group while serving as Louisiana State Treasurer?How much is The McKeon Group currently paying him?What work is Fleming currently performing for the firm?Which McKeon Group clients has Fleming advised, assisted, or worked on since becoming State Treasurer?Has Fleming sought ethics guidance or recused himself from any state matters involving McKeon Group clients?

Senator Collins questioned Kash Patel about illegal Chinese marijuana grow houses in Maine and whether the money from those operations is tied to drug trafficking. Peter, Texas Republicans are routinely taking orders from the outside instead of thinking for themselves about what Texas needs. The Governor takes cues and instructions from D.C. and forces them onto Republican legislators, who are powerless to resist (they know that if they resist, the Governor will finance their ouster in the next primary election). At times the legislators themselves get berated by the political thugs running the D.C. agenda, and find themselves forced to file bills without fully understanding what’s in them. The result is that anything that’s polling well with the Republican primary voting base gets rammed through and passed in a shamble of a process – suspended rules, hearings stuffed with misleading testimony, and rushed votes. The process becomes less about serving Texans and more about consolidating political power. The Texas Attorney General’s office is supposed to act as a check on this corrupt process. Current AG Ken Paxton has not only refused to act as a check, he’s facilitated it and participated in it. Paxton surrendered the independence of the OAG. Not very Texan, I say. The framers of the Texas Constitution understood the danger of concentrated power. That’s precisely why they made the Attorney General **an independently elected executive** office, with the charge and the authority to act as an independent check against corruption, unconstitutional laws, and abuse of power wherever it might occur. The final stage of the Democratic primary is almost here. We have two weeks left to ensure that we can restore public trust in this office. The result is that anything that’s polling well with the Republican primary voting base gets rammed through and passed in a shamble of a process – suspended rules, hearings stuffed with misleading testimony, and rushed votes. The process becomes less about serving Texans and more about consolidating political power. The Texas Attorney General’s office is supposed to act as a check on this corrupt process. Current AG Ken Paxton has not only refused to act as a check, he’s facilitated it and participated in it. Paxton surrendered the independence of the OAG. Not very Texan, I say. The framers of the Texas Constitution understood the danger of concentrated power. That’s precisely why they made the Attorney General an independently elected executive office, with the charge and the authority to act as an independent check against corruption, unconstitutional laws, and abuse of power wherever it might occur. body:

============================================================

Good afternoon!

We’re excited to invite you to the Grand Opening Celebration of the newly improved San Bruno Mountain Day Use Area!

Join San Mateo County Parks, California State Parks, and community members as we celebrate exciting new improvements that make this beautiful outdoor space more welcoming and accessible for everyone.

📅 Wednesday, May 13, 2026
⏰ 11:00 AM
📍 Saddle Area – San Bruno Mountain
555 Guadalupe Canyon Parkway, Brisbane, CA

The improvements include:
✅ ADA-accessible picnic areas
✅ Brand-new restroom facility
✅ Interpretive pavilion & displays
✅ Scenic mountain views
✅ Family-friendly outdoor gathering space

Enjoy a fun community ribbon-cutting celebration, photo opportunities, and the chance to explore one of our county’s most scenic outdoor destinations.

Bring a picnic, enjoy the fresh air, and celebrate this exciting park improvement project with us!

We hope to see you there. Please RSVP to Mike: ** mrichardson@smcgov.org (mailto:mrichardson@smcgov.org?subject=May%2013th%20Event%20)

David J. Canepa
San Mateo County Supervisor, District 5

# [This is backward](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=197222624&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk3MjIyNjI0LCJpYXQiOjE3Nzg2MjE1MDEsImV4cCI6MTc4MTIxMzUwMSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.cycvhcbjNuThNIcsBdBDe6PEKU_hDp7Q8afMhDVpQJc)
### MAGA priorities are making everything harder
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| May 12
---
| [](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9vcGVuLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9wdWIvaGFsZXlmb3JtaS9wL3RoaXMtaXMtYmFja3dhcmQ_.0Ny1QYoVDRzhdiT_p2ZA5Nio06KKKqSM9sqwMLhiSas?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/this-is-backward?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

I have a very simple question for Donald Trump and his Republican allies: **What happened to lowering prices?**
Because that's what they said they cared about, right? That's what we were told.
And yet here we are.
_Gas prices are climbing._
_Health care costs are rising._
_Manufacturing jobs are being cut._
_Rural hospitals are closing._
MAGA policies are forcing families across Michigan to do the thing that too many of us know all too well: sitting at the kitchen table with all the bills, pulling out a calculator, and trying to figure out what can wait, what can be stretched, and what just has to get paid this month.
**There are no good answers when the choice is between filling up your tank and buying groceries.**
But this is real life right now.
I talk to Michiganders every day who are struggling. And if that's you, I want you to know: I see you. I hear you. Please know this - you are the reason I'm in this fight.
**That 's why it makes me furious when Donald Trump says he doesn't care about hardworking Americans' financial situations. He actually said that.**
I'm sorry, WHAT?
Gas is nearly $5 a gallon in Michigan, and Trump doesn't care if folks can afford gas, groceries, or medication?
Truly, think about that. Who is MAGA fighting for then?
Not for the mom in Flint trying to fill up her tank on the way to work.
Not for the senior in Detroit worried about affording his prescriptions.
Not for the family in East Lansing who saw their health insurance premiums double.
Not for the worker in Kalamazoo who just got a letter saying the rent is going up again.
This is what I mean when I say MAGA priorities are upside down. Hardworking folks are genuinely struggling, and what are Republicans doing? Tax cuts for the rich. And pardons for Trump's friends.
I'm sorry, but that does not work for me. The government is supposed to work _for_ people.
That's why I've fought to lower costs and create jobs, expand programs like Medicare and Medicaid, and hold the Trump administration accountable on every front.
Friends, I'm in this fight for a basic idea that I think most Michiganders still believe in: If people are hurting, our leadership in Washington should help.
Call me crazy, but I do not think the Senate needs another politician who shrugs and goes along with Donald Trump's nonsense. That's not me.
**[I think Michigan needs somebody who will say, plainly: This is messed up. The way working people are struggling right now is unacceptable. Our leadership right now flat-out has the wrong priorities.](https://substack.com/redirect/41ae94ba-9c49-4395-83fa-4c6d05a4bd4e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
And I'm going to fight like hell to change them.
Because if gas is rising, health care costs are rising, jobs are disappearing, and hospitals are closing, then the answer is not "I don't care."
The answer is leadership that actually gives a damn about what regular working people are going through. And then taking action to help.
More soon.
With grit,
Haley

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131277092/620542228/1059865263?refcode=WUEFHQ39_20260512_TaylorLuriaSplit_ALL_v1s2&sourceid=1058717&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNRUwvMS84NzA2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyMmJiYmI3MS00YTRlLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Dyapc_LshOIbkZaNHMIAEP78LuL3Lu2zc8hi2thEp8o=) Peter,

Last month, millions of Virginians made their voices heard loud and clear, voting to push back against Donald Trump's gerrymandering across the country. But this past Friday, the Virginia Supreme Court decided to ignore those voices and struck down voter-approved congressional maps.

* * *
Max Miller isn't some random backbench congressman nobody's ever heard of. He's a former Trump aide. He's deeply embedded in the MAGA world. He got married at Trump's golf club with Donald Trump in attendance. Trump endorsed him. Elevated him. Helped build his career.
And now, after years of allegations from multiple women, after reports of violent behavior, after photographs of bruises, after accusations that incidents happened in front of a child, the Republican Party still closes ranks around him because proximity to Trump acts like a shield against accountability.
That's the real story.
Because this keeps happening.
Over and over and over again.
Every few months there's another Republican operative, another MAGA influencer, another congressman, another Trump ally accused of abuse, harassment, violence, coercion, or intimidation--and the response inside the movement is almost always the same:
Attack the accuser.
Question the victim.
Blame the media.
Protect the powerful man.
Move on.
And I need people to understand something: that culture doesn't emerge accidentally. It starts at the top.
Donald Trump has spent his entire public life teaching everyone around him that consequences are optional if you're rich enough, loyal enough, or useful enough. That's the operating principle of MAGA. Accountability is for other people.
That's why this feels bigger than one congressman.
Because if allegations like these had emerged about somebody outside the cult, Republicans would be screaming for resignations 24/7. Fox News would run wall-to-wall coverage. Every right-wing influencer on earth would suddenly become a champion for women and children.
But when it's one of their guys?
Silence.
Or worse, excuses.
And honestly, part of what makes this story so unbelievable is the fact that even having a United States senator as your father apparently still isn't enough protection from this culture. Think about that for a second. If the daughter of a Republican senator can allegedly be treated this way while the party circles the wagons around the accused, what message does that send to every other woman watching this unfold?
Because that's the other thing that keeps eating at me here: they don't even protect their own.
This is one of their own families. One of their own senators. One of their own daughters. And even then, the instinct inside this movement is still to defend the powerful man connected to Trump instead of demanding accountability.
How broken do you have to be as a political movement for that to become normal?
And what keeps bothering me most about this story is the child.
Because according to these reports, some of these alleged incidents happened in front of a two-year-old little girl.
As a parent, I can't shake that.
I cannot imagine putting fear into a child like that. I cannot imagine creating an environment where a kid grows up watching violence, chaos, screaming, intimidation -- whatever allegedly happened behind those doors. That kind of trauma doesn't just disappear because adults decide to spin the headlines later.
And this is why accountability matters early.
And honestly, the part of this story that scares me the most isn't even necessarily what we know -- it's what we _don 't_ know.
Every time somebody powerful is accused of abuse, you have to wonder how many other people stayed silent out of fear. How many staffers, exes, friends, or victims convinced themselves it wasn't worth speaking up because they knew the machine would protect him anyway?
That's the pattern with powerful men inside movements like this. The public allegations are usually just the surface. The truly disturbing part is wondering how much behavior never sees daylight because the people involved don't have the resources, platform, or protection to fight back.
Because systems that protect powerful men create more dangerous men.
If somebody learns over and over again that money, status, political connections, and intimidation can save them from consequences, the behavior escalates. That's true in politics. That's true in Hollywood. That's true everywhere.
And frankly, that's been the story of Trumpism from the beginning.
The movement rewards cruelty.
It rewards dominance.
It rewards intimidation.
It rewards people willing to bully, humiliate, threaten, and steamroll others in pursuit of power.
Then everybody acts surprised when the people attracted to that culture turn out to be abusive in private too.
Really?
What exactly did people think was going to happen?
Because this isn't just about one "bad apple." It's about a political ecosystem where morality is entirely conditional. If you help the movement win, almost anything gets rationalized away.
And before somebody says, "Well, both parties have bad people," yes--obviously. Throw every abuser out. Every single one. I don't care what letter is next to their name.
But only one political movement in America currently treats accountability itself as the enemy.
Only one movement consistently turns powerful men accused of horrific behavior into martyrs.
Only one movement seems fundamentally incapable of saying, "If this is true, this person should never hold power again."
That's the rot.
That's the sickness underneath all of this.
And until this country stops rewarding people for cruelty, until voters stop excusing behavior they would never tolerate in their own homes, until political parties fear protecting abusers more than they fear losing power, these stories are going to keep happening.
That's the part that disgusts me most.
Not that monsters exist.
But that so many powerful people keep helping them survive.

name: AOC
subject: My thoughts on the filibuster
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
The filibuster isn’t sacred
#
At the University of Chicago, David Axelrod asked me whether I would do away with the filibuster.
I do not appreciate the wholesale fictionalization of American history — the idea that the filibuster is a grand compromise intentionally put into our system.
The filibuster in the Senate was created by a clerical error, and Jim Crow segregationists realized that they could use it to delay the enfranchisement of Black Americans for decades.
**The origin of the filibuster is part of the institutional racism that was baked into our institutions.**
The idea that it was a high-minded, intentional mechanism is just a fairytale meant to launder the history of racism in America into something it’s not.
We have to have a politics of integrity. We have to stand up for what is right in this country. **We can change the page.**
Together, we’ve built a movement fighting for critical issues — from Medicare for All to democratizing fundraising power in politics.
[Help us continue the fight for racial, social, economic and environmental justice with a grassroots contribution today.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260512.dtn8Yk&refcode=em20260512-11404-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=11404%2E2526796%2ESzlsZi)

In solidarity,
Alexandria

clean_body: When the MAGA justices arrive at the Capitol on May 20th, they’ll see our signs and hear our voices. | | Peter, On May 20th, the Supreme Court justices are headed to the Capitol to request more taxpayer dollars. It’s the first time the justices have testified in committee in 15 years—and it comes just weeks after the Supreme Court’s decision gutting voting rights and rigging the midterm elections. We cannot allow Congress to treat this like business as usual. We deserve answers. We deserve for our demands to be heard. We deserve a democracy that’s built for us, not the wannabe dictator and the wealthy extremists pulling the strings. That’s why we’re rallying outside the Capitol on May 20th. When the MAGA justices arrive to testify, they’ll see our signs and hear our voices. They’ll be forced to realize that We the People are paying attention. Together, we’re sending a clear message that our communities will not stay silent while representation and voting rights are undermined. ** Everyday, working families across the country are struggling to afford gas, groceries, rent, healthcare, and childcare. They’re facing ICE terror in the streets. They’re watching our power be ripped from us and handed directly to the billionaires and corporations making our lives harder. The MAGA justices on the Supreme Court have only made things worse. They’ve ruled in Trump’s favor 90% of the time. They made it possible for wealthy extremists to rig the system. It’s up to We the People to demand accountability, an end to corruption and unchecked power, and a system that actually works for our communities. They work for us! This is about more than just one court decision. It’s about whether our democracy still belongs to the people. Peter,

My name is Adam Schwarze, and I'm a former Navy SEAL, Marine Corps veteran, and proud Minnesotan **running for U.S. Senate against Tim Walz's handpicked lieutenant governor—a politician even more radical than her boss.** I'm requesting your support in this critical battle to restore common-sense conservative values to Minnesota.

I hold a Master's from Harvard, a Master's Certificate from Johns Hopkins in Security and Nuclear Deterrence, and an MBA. I’ve faced worse odds overseas and am ready to bring that same grit to Washington | Peter, My name is Adam Schwarze, and I'm a former Navy SEAL, Marine Corps veteran, and proud Minnesotan running for U.S. Senate against Tim Walz's handpicked lieutenant governor—a politician even more radical than her boss. I'm requesting your support in this critical battle to restore common-sense conservative values to Minnesota. I hold a Master's from Harvard, a Master's Certificate from Johns Hopkins in Security and Nuclear Deterrence, and an MBA. But my proudest achievement is serving our country to make my parents, especially my mom, proud. I want to serve you in the U.S. Senate, fighting for the values that have made Minnesota and America great for generations. I'm starting this race with absolutely nothing , but because of the enormity of the race's outcome, I figured there is no harm in asking for your help. At the end of the day, my request of you will end in one of two ways: 1.) . 2.) you read this email without contributing, but you at least now know who I am. I'm not a career politician. I'm a regular guy from a working-class family who grew up playing hockey and answered our nation's call on my 18th birthday in October 2001, just weeks after the 9/11 attacks. I joined the Marine Corps to defend our country, and as a Navy SEAL, I deployed nine times to over 70 countries, risking my life to protect our freedoms and way of life. Unlike Tim Walz, who retired from the National Guard before his unit deployed to Iraq, I never backed down from serving our nation during war. Minnesota is at a crossroads. Under Governor Walz and his lieutenant governor, our state has been dragged left by radical policies that fueled the violent unrest in Minneapolis in 2020, defunded our police , and burdened hardworking families with higher taxes and inflation. While our streets burned, the lieutenant governor pushed lawsuits against law enforcement, undermining the officers keeping us safe. This isn't the Minnesota I grew up in—or the one any Minnesotan deserves. If you are reading this email right now and you don't live in Minnesota, then I'm sure you'll agree with me that every American must be represented by individuals in Congress who want to build a better version of the America we live in today—individuals of integrity. That's not who my opponent is. We have an incredible opportunity to elect a Republican to the U.S. Senate next year - something voters in this state haven't done since they re-elected former Senator Norm Coleman in 2002. As a Republican, I know the odds are tough in a state that hasn't voted red in a presidential election since 1976. But as a former Navy SEAL, I thrive in tough fights. I've faced worse odds overseas and am ready to bring that same grit to Washington. Here's what I stand for: Restoring law and order by supporting our police and cracking down on crime. Cutting taxes and regulations to ease the burden on retirees and small businesses. Securing our borders to protect our communities and sovereignty. Defending our Second Amendment rights and traditional values. Stopping the radical left's agenda that's eroding the America we love. You don't know me, but you know what men like me stand for and our reputation. So, . This race won't be easy. The Democrats have deep pockets, and the radical left will stop at nothing to keep this seat. I'm running to serve you, to protect our way of life, and to ensure Minnesota remains a place where faith, family, and freedom thrive. I hope you'll invest in me right now – any amount will help. UPDATE FROM DELEGATE HAMILTON!
---
| |
---
| VIRGINIA IS FOR PATRIOTS!
---
---
---
---
| Hamilton Headlines It's been an eventful couple of weeks in Virginia! The Supreme Court of Virginia ruled the redistricting referendum unconstitutional in a 4-3 vote! Their focus was on the process of amending the Constitution. In Virginia, the process of amending the Constitution is deliberately slow. An amendment must pass through the General Assembly in TWO consecutive sessions, with an intervening general election IN-BETWEEN, before being sent to the public for a vote. Democrats did not have a complete intervening election because early voting was well underway. Almost 1 million Virginians had already voted, with no knowledge of the redistricting amendment. Therefore, the courts rightly ruled the process UNCONSTITUTIONAL.
---
|
---
In other news, President Pro Tempore of the Senate, L. Louise Lucas became the target of an FBI investigation that orginated under the Biden Administration. While the findings of this are unknown, speculation is swirling with questions of potential corruption, bribery or illegal activities, either in her cannabis dispensary businesses or her medicaid dependent home health care businesses. Senator Lucas is among the most powerful Democrats in Virginia, and the seen by many as the most forceful negotiator concerning the budget. Speaking of the budget... It has been 59 days since session adjourned, and Democrats have still not been able to produce a balanced budget. The negative ripple effects of this are felt in every district across the Commonwealth, as local boards work to finalize their own budgets. There are reports of counties delaying the renewal of teacher contracts until they receive the final budget from Richmond. These are the real life consequences of dysfunctional governance. The data center tax break remains the primary point of contention. The Senate is fighting to eliminate the data center tax break while the House Democrats and Governor would like to keep it.
|
---
Much of the legislation that passed under the Democrat trifecta this year was not designed with rural Virginia or your family in mind. Here is what passed — and why it matters to you: Collective Bargaining Mandates (HB1263, SB378):These bills strip local governments of the flexibility to manage their own workforces and budgets. Counties are anticipating real estate taxes increasing by 30 to 40 cents per $100 of home value to cover the cost of this unfunded mandate. Criminal Justice Changes (HB361, HB637, HB863):Sentencing standards were weakened and penalties reduced. I will always stand with law enforcement and with victims. These changes move us in the wrong direction. Energy & Data Centers (HB153, HB496, HB1444, HB397):Rapid, unchecked growth threatens rural Virginia. They call it "progress" — until it's your land, your electric bill, and your community bearing the costs. Grid reliability and affordability were not adequately addressed. Second Amendment Restrictions (HB1524, HB21, HB702, HB201):I will never stop defending your constitutional rights. These bills do nothing to stop violence. They expand regulations and burdens on law-abiding gun owners — people who have done nothing wrong. HB217 (firearm ban) was returned to Governor and is awaiting signature or veto by May 22nd deadline. Keep reminding Governor Spanberger of your opinion on this unconstitutional bill! This was a frustrating session, but I will continue to fight for district 62 in Richmond— for local control, parental rights in education, law enforcement, constitutional freedoms, and responsible stewardship of your tax dollars. As always, I am guided by faith, grateful for your trust, and honored to serve, Greene, Madison, Orange, and Culpeper. Karen HamiltonDelegate62nd District

Virginia Democrats just floated a crazy plan to fire every Supreme Court justice that ruled against them.
[And right here at home](https://us.list-manage.com/keLVAM6C5a0?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e), a polling memo just landed on Gabe Vasquez — and his numbers are upside down.

🏛️ **VIRGINIA DEMS WANT TO RETIRE EVERY SUPREME COURT JUSTICE AT 54**
The state Supreme Court ruled 4-3 against their gerrymandered map. So on a private call this past weekend with Hakeem Jeffries, House Democrats started floating a fix.
Lower the mandatory retirement age to exactly the age of the youngest justice. Every vote in the majority is gone overnight. Replace them with friendlier judges. Reinstate the map.
One Virginia Democrat has already gone on record supporting it. Jonathan Turley calls it "murderball." We explain what Governor Spanberger has to decide — and what happens if she signs.

💰 **THE POLLING MEMO ON GABE VASQUEZ IS UGLY**
The NRCC just dropped a memo on the Vasquez seat. Generic ballot? Dead even. Vasquez's favorability? Underwater. The Democratic Party brand in his district? Worse.
Greg Cunningham trails by two — and nobody knows him yet.
National Republican money is moving in. We explain why this is the best Republican opportunity in the state, and what has to happen for Cunningham to actually close it.

🏛️ **NM GOV "HOT SEAT" — TURNER, HULL, AND DUKE TAKE THE TOUGHEST QUESTIONS**
Elias Sisneros moderated a forum at Legacy Church and gave each Republican candidate the one question they didn't want.
Doug Turner faced his firm's state COVID contract. Gregg Hull faced his fundraising. Duke Rodriguez faced his history of writing checks to Democrats.
One answer was solid. One was honest in a way that worried us. One was bravado that didn't land. We break down all three.

🚨 **1 IN 4 "VERY LIBERAL" AMERICANS: POLITICAL FORCE IS SOMETIMES JUSTIFIED**
A new YouGov poll dropped, and the breakdown is a gut punch.
11% of all US adults say political force is sometimes justified. Among "very liberal" Americans? It jumps to 25%. Among liberals under 45? 26%.
When you put that number next to what's happening in Virginia right now, the connection is hard to miss.

# **Trump warns US-Iran ceasefire has "1% chance" of survival as nuclear talks stall**
President Donald Trump **[told reporters Monday](https://substack.com/redirect/4d790fd7-db8b-455a-a36e-3272efb39ec8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** the ceasefire is "on massive life support" after rejecting an Iranian proposal that delayed nuclear program negotiations while focusing on ending the U.S. blockade, saying "I have a plan. Iran can't have a nuclear weapon." Trump said U.S. officials believe Iran previously agreed to relinquish enriched uranium stockpiles but the regime's latest response omitted any reference to the issue, suggesting Tehran's position may have shifted.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7746b1e8-cbec-406e-9c5f-02f08ae1ed21?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Military analysts outline escalation path if diplomacy fails** : Retired Army Col. Seth Krummrich told Fox News negotiations face deep mistrust with "neither side trust[ing] each other at all," while retired Air Force Lt. Gen. David Deptula said any renewed conflict would become "a contest for escalation control" targeting Iran's ballistic missiles, air defenses, maritime assets, IRGC infrastructure and nuclear facilities to deny Tehran "the tools it uses to escalate."
* **The U.S. struck Iran 's Qeshm port and Bandar Abbas** Thursday after Iran fired 15 missiles at UAE's Fujairah Port, though officials insisted the operation didn't restart the war.
* **Experts warn seizing Iranian uranium would be "extreme risk" operation**: Retired Rear Adm. Mark Montgomery said Washington should "squeeze them for at least another three to six weeks" economically before broadening military action, though Trump has warned the U.S. could target electric plants, oil infrastructure and export hubs like Kharg Island if talks fail.

* * *
# **ICE uncovers massive fraud in foreign student work program, finds empty buildings claiming hundreds of employees**
Acting ICE Director Todd Lyons **[announced Tuesday](https://substack.com/redirect/e6ba6634-3f17-4fb0-8c72-da0f09cc8fc6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that investigators discovered extensive fraud in the Optional Practical Training program, which permits international students to gain work experience in their academic fields while residing in the U.S.
* **What they found:** Federal agents visiting supposed employment locations found vacant buildings purportedly housing hundreds of workers, residential properties with no business operations despite being listed as job sites, and companies sharing addresses without actual leases--prompting Lyons to warn the scheme represents just "the tip of the iceberg" in what he called an "uncontrolled guest worker pipeline."
* **North Texas investigation reveals suspicious employer networks, Houston "pay to stay" scheme**: Last week's sweep of 18 north Texas locations uncovered clusters of businesses operating from the same complexes with nearly identical online presences and overlapping management yet claiming independence from each other, according to Homeland Security Investigations Acting Executive Associate Director John Condon. Houston agents identified a company charging students secretly to help them illegally maintain visa status, while a New Jersey business supposedly supporting over 150 foreign workers couldn't provide basic information about their identities or job duties.
* **Lyons vows prosecutions for "deliberate, coordinated, and criminal" activity**: The ICE director described the fraud as systematic and intentional, promising increased scrutiny at overseas consulates for trafficking, forced labor and document fraud among student visa applicants. Many fraudulent employers showed warning signs including tax debts, lawsuit judgments and contract violations, with some students never actually reporting to jobs they claimed.

Friend, Corporate money has no place in our politics―at any level. But whether it’s the U.S. Supreme Court opening the floodgates to big money in politics through its disastrous _Citizens United_ decision, or state laws that allow corporate donations to candidates, corporate PACs have been flooding our elections, seeking to ensure elected officials put corporate profits over the needs of our communities. In my home state of Michigan, DTE Energy spends millions of dollars influencing state lawmakers―and according to 2024 public filing disclosures, donated to 120 out of 148 state lawmakers through shadow political committees in the last election. **They use their influence to raise our residents’ rates―enriching their wealthy shareholders instead of improving access and service.** That’s why I’m standing with Michiganders for Money Out of Politics, working to break up the current pay-to-play system by banning utilities and corporations with large state or local government contracts from donating to candidates. **Michiganders for Money Out of Politics (MMOP) is organizing to get a proposal on the November ballot to get corporate money out of politics.** Over 80% of Michigan voters approve of this solution. But before we can vote on it, MMOP needs to collect and submit more than 350,000 signatures―and they’re close! [**Donate to Michiganders for Money Out of Politics and help get them across the finish line, submitting the signatures needed to put this critical proposal on the ballot and get corporate money out of politics.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3_id01L9i6Msk2rgA893UkWXSnnG22EYYKipICK6pnGw1JVoEBFzN2cmJns2oOJTnWghP6kyowv4b10Jj2W9FsRcROQ5F0aAHdgVtCTKWakHu8OnNb1gMjh64cuEAb4RbBilqOOeBcOcti3NK8RSf5o96nJVTS6wUpuXLC1jpN-XzDVDwucLM9OEMND3sFWuaFLOUw-gno9g3KQYg_RFGPdZxjjYsqVH-E2zI9jFKXfhRfcS01XZFN-dScpJgDOjoA/4qk/wo9_WvZfQASqKzLeZDhcZw/h1/h001.GhWPh3KMVK0qEGX1gUoFF-33rE2qEycNAKYWs_Qkwr0) | [DONATE](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3_id01L9i6Msk2rgA893UkWXSnnG22EYYKipICK6pnGw1JVoEBFzN2cmJns2oOJTnVioqyj_Ex8aDQfzD4bLLm5O0iF6L7ucsCbpUFsxypzFijyaGwMWPl-pUflFi3LFHVqRgroXw-AgrcrXZTEEocQnrhajyua4lrKf0n-9UOvt2MnnOqZRi0ILUPlwooGWvuWMnYDoAg42GzbwVZtkGijD6q3CESO9zxHKk4h1dpkD7863T_RyQMdu2trDfGRz7M/4qk/wo9_WvZfQASqKzLeZDhcZw/h2/h001.jAfo71eDzAvt_BQWM_189A5dIqmFB9pVLIDFY3xRShg)

This pattern is happening in states around the country. **Utilities are poisoning our communities by burning fossil fuels, blocking renewable energy, hijacking our state governments, and prioritizing profits over families.**
Our residents deserve a political system that puts our needs ahead of the profits of greedy, polluting corporations.
Even though DTE keeps raising rates, it has failed to invest in critical infrastructure updates, leaving our neighbors with long and frequent power outages.

clean_body: Our residents deserve a political system that puts our needs ahead of the profits of greedy, polluting corporations. | | | Friend, Corporate money has no place in our politics―at any level. But whether it’s the U.S. Supreme Court opening the floodgates to big money in politics through its disastrous Citizens United decision, or state laws that allow corporate donations to candidates, corporate PACs have been flooding our elections, seeking to ensure elected officials put corporate profits over the needs of our communities. In my home state of Michigan, DTE Energy spends millions of dollars influencing state lawmakers―and according to 2024 public filing disclosures, donated to 120 out of 148 state lawmakers through shadow political committees in the last election. They use their influence to raise our residents’ rates―enriching their wealthy shareholders instead of improving access and service. That’s why I’m standing with Michiganders for Money Out of Politics, working to break up the current pay-to-play system by banning utilities and corporations with large state or local government contracts from donating to candidates. Michiganders for Money Out of Politics (MMOP) is organizing to get a proposal on the November ballot to get corporate money out of politics. Over 80% of Michigan voters approve of this solution. But before we can vote on it, MMOP needs to collect and submit more than 350,000 signatures―and they’re close! | For years, DTE Energy has been raking in profits for its wealthy shareholders and buying off politicians in order to evade accountability. This pattern is happening in states around the country. Utilities are poisoning our communities by burning fossil fuels, blocking renewable energy, hijacking our state governments, and prioritizing profits over families. Our residents deserve a political system that puts our needs ahead of the profits of greedy, polluting corporations. Even though DTE keeps raising rates, it has failed to invest in critical infrastructure updates, leaving our neighbors with long and frequent power outages. I promise to continue to hold corporations accountable and fight for our right to affordable and reliable utility services. body:
Meet Leila, Spencer, and Dinah.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260512-1&t=1&akid=3470%2E587540%2EHUbp8t)
Exciting news, Peter!
**Leaders We Deserve is proud to announce we’re officially endorsing:**
**⭐ Leila Staton** for Iowa HD-54
**⭐ Spencer Dixon** for Maryland HD-32
**⭐ Dinah Escarment** for Florida HD-108
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260512_1_state.kRoy7W&refcode=em20260512-3470&t=2&akid=3470%2E587540%2EHUbp8t)
Before I tell you about each of them — state legislatures play a major role in shaping the reality of people’s everyday lives. They’re where abortion bans get blocked or passed, where Medicaid gets expanded or gutted, where working families either get a seat at the table or get left out entirely while corporations write the rules. That’s why Leaders We Deserve backs bold, people-powered candidates to run in them.
**[Will you split a $5 donation between Leila, Spencer, Dinah, and Leaders We Deserve today to help power their campaigns?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260512_1_state.kRoy7W&refcode=em20260512-3470&amount=5&t=3&akid=3470%2E587540%2EHUbp8t)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260512_1_state.kRoy7W&amount=5&refcode=em20260512-3470&t=4&akid=3470%2E587540%2EHUbp8t)**
**Leila Staton** has been showing up for her community her entire life. Whether it was cleaning up local parks or volunteering with her local fire department, she’s always been dedicated to public service. As a child sexual assault advocate, she’s been a fierce voice for survivors in her community. And she co-founded Insufferable Wenches of Iowa, a local progressive organizing group that has been delivering mutual aid and civic education to communities across the district.
In Des Moines, Leila will fight to fix Iowa’s water quality crisis — the state’s cancer rate has been rising as agricultural runoff poisons local water supply. She’ll fight to protect public schools from the voucher program draining funding from communities that need it most, and expand access to affordable healthcare and housing for every Iowan. And she’ll protect local farms from out-of-state corporations trying to gobble up family land.
Her opponent, Joshua Meggers, is an extremely conservative Republican who has backed anti-abortion legislation, voted to strip gender identity protections from Iowa’s Civil Rights Act, and championed cutting corporate taxes while working families in his district struggled to get by. This district runs red, but Leila is exactly the kind of candidate who puts it into play, because she’s been building bridges and fighting for her community long before this race.
**[Split a Donation](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260512_1_state.kRoy7W&amount=5&refcode=em20260512-3470&t=5&akid=3470%2E587540%2EHUbp8t)**
**Spencer Dixon** grew up in Anne Arundel County when the 2008 financial crisis hit his family hard. He watched his mother fight with greedy insurance companies after being diagnosed with a chronic illness before the ACA protected people with pre-existing conditions. That experience lit a fire under him. He went on to serve as Legislative Director in the Maryland State Senate, learning firsthand how to navigate the system and fight for the people it too often ignores. Now he works at the Maryland Prescription Drug Affordability Board, fighting to lower the cost of medicine for Marylanders. He also chairs Anne Arundel County’s Public Campaign Financing Commission, working to level the playing field for grassroots candidates and get corporate money out of local politics.
In Annapolis, Spencer will invest in clean energy to lower utility bills, and make sure data centers pay their fair share of energy costs instead of passing it off to working families. He’ll protect Marylanders from this administration’s cuts to Medicaid and food assistance, fight back against corporate landlords using dynamic pricing to drive up rent, reopen Maryland’s Child Care Scholarship Program, and push for full funding of the Blueprint for Maryland’s future, a decade-long plan to transform public education.
This is a safe blue seat, but Spencer is running in a four-way primary. With his primary coming up fast on **June 23** , he’ll need real resources to cut through the crowded field. But he has the experience and a proven record of fighting for working Marylanders — so this race is his to win.
**[Split a Donation](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260512_1_state.kRoy7W&amount=5&refcode=em20260512-3470&t=6&akid=3470%2E587540%2EHUbp8t)**
**Dinah Escarment** is a Democratic State Committeewoman and relentless advocate for South Florida’s Haitian community. Her 6 years teaching students from low-income communities in Broward and Orange County public schools shaped her commitment to expanding opportunity for those Florida politicians were too eager to leave behind. She currently chairs Florida Rising — a grassroots organization building political power in Black and Brown communities across the state — and serves as Vice President of the Miami-Dade County Democratic Haitian Caucus.
In Tallahassee, Dinah will fight to protect immigrant communities from ICE’s terror and push back against the Trump administration’s assault on TPS holders. She’ll expand access to affordable housing, strengthen tenant protections for working families being priced out of their neighborhoods, invest in public schools, bring reliable access to healthcare to underserved communities, and create youth programs and mentorship opportunities so that every student has the chance to thrive.
District 108 is a safe blue seat, and Dinah stands in stark contrast to her opponent, Daphne Campbell. As a State Rep., Campbell was the only Florida House Democrat to vote for a mandatory waiting period for abortions. And during Hurricane Irma, she used her political connections to jump ahead in the power restoration line while her own constituents sat in the dark. This district deserves leadership who will truly put their community first — and Dinah is ready to offer them just that.
**[Split a Donation](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260512_1_state.kRoy7W&amount=5&refcode=em20260512-3470&t=7&akid=3470%2E587540%2EHUbp8t)**
**Leila, Spencer, and Dinah are exactly the kind of candidates Leaders We Deserve was built to back.** Courageous, deeply rooted in their communities, and not beholden to any corporate donors or special interests. But these leaders need your support to win.
**[If you’re able, can you split a $5 donation between Leila, Spencer, Dinah, and Leaders We Deserve today?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260512_1_state.kRoy7W&refcode=em20260512-3470&amount=5&t=8&akid=3470%2E587540%2EHUbp8t)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260512_1_state.kRoy7W&amount=5&refcode=em20260512-3470&t=27&akid=3470%2E587540%2EHUbp8t)**
Thank you,
David Hogg

_**By David Shuster**_
In the United States under Trump, there are few spectacles as predictable and sad as the sight of Americans being robbed twice and told to applaud the billionaire class efficiency.
The latest pathetic gag involves the Trump administration's grand tariff crusade. As you may recall, Dementia Don and his sycophants insisted that taxing imports was a clever way to make foreigners suffer. The foreigner, of course, suffered very little. American consumers, as usual, got punched in the kidneys.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4a3af288-b7a9-445c-8172-e9e9af41b379?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.-vapoM_uoS8zvQWqbPy9B2UL6hYVOmDZwBMT9b67ikQ?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=197268649)
That's because when Trump imposed his tariffs, or "liberation day" as he called it, nearly every U.S. industrialist and import business claimed victimhood. "Costs are rising," they insisted. "Supply chains are strained! Sacrifices are necessary for the national good." So, most U.S. corporations raised prices. Automobile sticker costs climbed upwards, along with household appliances, food, and nearly every manufactured contraption or product that required foreign assembly or foreign inputs.
And who paid? The clueless consumer in the showroom. The shopper in the grocery store. The citizen who imagined already profitable billion dollar corporations would absorb taxes out of civic tenderness.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4a3af288-b7a9-445c-8172-e9e9af41b379?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

The companies themselves absorbed almost nothing except the proceeds.
Then came the judiciary, solemn as always and generally late to every fire. The U.S. Supreme Court, after permitting the tariff carnival to run long enough for nearly every corporation to raise prices for almost a year, finally struck down the tariffs.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4a3af288-b7a9-445c-8172-e9e9af41b379?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Three conservative justices, in a rare moment acknowledging reality, joined liberal justices in declaring the U.S. was not facing an economic emergency as Trump had claimed.
The Supreme Court ruling, in turn, has now triggered an immense cascade of tariff refunds -- not to the citizens who paid the inflated prices, but to the corporations that already collected them.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4a3af288-b7a9-445c-8172-e9e9af41b379?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.-vapoM_uoS8zvQWqbPy9B2UL6hYVOmDZwBMT9b67ikQ?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=197268649)
And here comes the punch line. The Trump administration, with its habit for converting larceny into policy, is preparing to refund roughly $166 billion in tariffs to the very corporations that already collected the money from the public. One might as well reimburse a bank robber for wear and tear on his ransom notes.
Ford, we are informed, expects a return of some $1.3 billion. General Motors anticipates another $500 million. And what noble purpose shall this torrent of cash serve? Will it be distributed among customers who paid tariff-bloated prices? Will the automakers reduce the price of vehicles being sold now? Will Ford and GM ease the financial burdens of citizens whose bank accounts were squeezed in the first place?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4a3af288-b7a9-445c-8172-e9e9af41b379?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=197268649&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk3MjY4NjQ5LCJpYXQiOjE3Nzg2Mjc3ODMsImV4cCI6MTc4MTIxOTc4MywiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.beEgy-NJYltOdGlt6wTgljtruQbCWMfbw7htTeA3GKE)
Of course not. The automakers, like other corporations receiving tariff refunds from the Trump administration, say they will deposit the tariff money in their own accounts to "boost earnings."
Thus, we have the whole majestic farce. The public pays inflated prices while corporate titans lecture us about patriotism. Then, the Trump Treasury sends the corporations a handsome rebate for expenses they already passed along to the public. Finally, the same corporations announce improved quarterly earnings, and the conservative financial press hails the triumph as evidence of managerial brilliance.
The American consumer, meanwhile, stands blinking in the smoke like a peasant who has just watched all his or her possessions loaded into the back of a thief's wagon with nothing left behind but a receipt.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4a3af288-b7a9-445c-8172-e9e9af41b379?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[Leave a comment](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=197268649&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&isFreemail=true&comments=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk3MjY4NjQ5LCJpYXQiOjE3Nzg2Mjc3ODMsImV4cCI6MTc4MTIxOTc4MywiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.beEgy-NJYltOdGlt6wTgljtruQbCWMfbw7htTeA3GKE&r=1hvr60&utm_campaign=email-half-magic-comments&action=post-comment)
The truth is that tariffs have always been a crafty device for transferring wealth upward while disguising the process in patriotic bunting. Tariffs are sold to the masses as punishment for foreigners. But the foreigner somehow never seems to pay. Instead, the bill arrives at the local dealership, the toy store, and the kitchen table. The citizen, through what is essentially a consumption tax, finances the entire enterprise and is then invited to celebrate the fleecing as an act of national economic vigor.
And the insults keep coming. Because now, the corporations are going to be paid again. Their CEO's will be granted even more obscenely high reward packages. The corporate investors and speculators who trade pieces of paper (or digital transactions) representing company shares will also make more money. After all, higher corporate earnings mean more stock value.
It's like Robin Hood upside down, in reverse, and on steroids.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4a3af288-b7a9-445c-8172-e9e9af41b379?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.-vapoM_uoS8zvQWqbPy9B2UL6hYVOmDZwBMT9b67ikQ?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=197268649)
But this time, it's not the poor who benefit from Robin, Friar Tuck, and Little John. The benefactors are the wealthiest 1%, including corporate CEO's, hedge fund managers, and corporate speculators.
Once again, America has tilted the personal financial playing field in favor of the haves at the expense of the have nots.
Consider what the United States could have done with the $166 billion the Trump treasury department is now transferring back in tariff refunds to already successful corporations.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4a3af288-b7a9-445c-8172-e9e9af41b379?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=197268649&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk3MjY4NjQ5LCJpYXQiOjE3Nzg2Mjc3ODMsImV4cCI6MTc4MTIxOTc4MywiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.beEgy-NJYltOdGlt6wTgljtruQbCWMfbw7htTeA3GKE)
We could have funded WIC - the nutrition program foe infants and mothers, for 20 years.
Or, we could have provided housing, for 15 years, for every person who is currently homeless.
Or, we could have funded Head Start, the preschool program for disadvantaged kids, for 12 years.
Or, we could have funded SNAP or "food stamp" benefits for 8 years. (Trump's One Big Beautiful bill cut the SNAP program.)
Or, we could have given every person in America a check of $474.
Instead, we get nothing. And corporate America gets it all.
It is Trump style capitalism with the Orange Man's smile and his family's usual ethics. Heads the billionaire class wins, tails the public loses twice. And somewhere in the distance, one can almost hear the applause from Wall Street as ordinary Americans stand in the checkout line financing yet another victory parade for people who already own the floats.

David Shuster on the Robin Hood scam in reverse. | | and | May 12 | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- By David Shuster In the United States under Trump, there are few spectacles as predictable and sad as the sight of Americans being robbed twice and told to applaud the billionaire class efficiency. The latest pathetic gag involves the Trump administration's grand tariff crusade. As you may recall, Dementia Don and his sycophants insisted that taxing imports was a clever way to make foreigners suffer. The foreigner, of course, suffered very little. American consumers, as usual, got punched in the kidneys. | | ---|---|--- That's because when Trump imposed his tariffs, or "liberation day" as he called it, nearly every U.S. industrialist and import business claimed victimhood. "Costs are rising," they insisted. "Supply chains are strained! Sacrifices are necessary for the national good." So, most U.S. corporations raised prices. Automobile sticker costs climbed upwards, along with household appliances, food, and nearly every manufactured contraption or product that required foreign assembly or foreign inputs. And who paid? The clueless consumer in the showroom. The shopper in the grocery store. The citizen who imagined already profitable billion dollar corporations would absorb taxes out of civic tenderness. | | ---|---|--- The companies themselves absorbed almost nothing except the proceeds. Then came the judiciary, solemn as always and generally late to every fire. The U.S. Supreme Court, after permitting the tariff carnival to run long enough for nearly every corporation to raise prices for almost a year, finally struck down the tariffs. | | ---|---|--- Three conservative justices, in a rare moment acknowledging reality, joined liberal justices in declaring the U.S. was not facing an economic emergency as Trump had claimed. The Supreme Court ruling, in turn, has now triggered an immense cascade of tariff refunds -- not to the citizens who paid the inflated prices, but to the corporations that already collected them. | | ---|---|--- And here comes the punch line. The Trump administration, with its habit for converting larceny into policy, is preparing to refund roughly $166 billion in tariffs to the very corporations that already collected the money from the public. One might as well reimburse a bank robber for wear and tear on his ransom notes. Ford, we are informed, expects a return of some $1.3 billion. General Motors anticipates another $500 million. And what noble purpose shall this torrent of cash serve? Will it be distributed among customers who paid tariff-bloated prices? Will the automakers reduce the price of vehicles being sold now? Will Ford and GM ease the financial burdens of citizens whose bank accounts were squeezed in the first place? | | ---|---|--- Of course not. The automakers, like other corporations receiving tariff refunds from the Trump administration, say they will deposit the tariff money in their own accounts to "boost earnings." Thus, we have the whole majestic farce. The public pays inflated prices while corporate titans lecture us about patriotism. Then, the Trump Treasury sends the corporations a handsome rebate for expenses they already passed along to the public. Finally, the same corporations announce improved quarterly earnings, and the conservative financial press hails the triumph as evidence of managerial brilliance. The American consumer, meanwhile, stands blinking in the smoke like a peasant who has just watched all his or her possessions loaded into the back of a thief's wagon with nothing left behind but a receipt. | | ---|---|--- The truth is that tariffs have always been a crafty device for transferring wealth upward while disguising the process in patriotic bunting. Tariffs are sold to the masses as punishment for foreigners. But the foreigner somehow never seems to pay. Instead, the bill arrives at the local dealership, the toy store, and the kitchen table. The citizen, through what is essentially a consumption tax, finances the entire enterprise and is then invited to celebrate the fleecing as an act of national economic vigor. And the insults keep coming. Because now, the corporations are going to be paid again. Their CEO's will be granted even more obscenely high reward packages. The corporate investors and speculators who trade pieces of paper (or digital transactions) representing company shares will also make more money. After all, higher corporate earnings mean more stock value. It's like Robin Hood upside down, in reverse, and on steroids. | | ---|---|--- But this time, it's not the poor who benefit from Robin, Friar Tuck, and Little John. The benefactors are the wealthiest 1%, including corporate CEO's, hedge fund managers, and corporate speculators. Once again, America has tilted the personal financial playing field in favor of the haves at the expense of the have nots. [1]LeftNet

Over the past few months, I’ve spent a lot of time listening, reflecting,
and thinking about what this moment demands of us.

What I keep coming back to is this: people are looking for leadership that
shows up, tells the truth, and is willing to fight for what matters. I’ve
run in tough places. I’ve won in tough places. And I still believe the
path forward is the same as it’s always been: go where the fight is, say
what you believe, and make the case everywhere.

That’s why I’m launching Small Town PAC.

I believe small towns still matter. The people in them still matter. And
if Democrats want to build a stronger party, we’ve got to be willing to
show up, listen, organize, and compete in more places. We can’t keep
writing off communities and expect to start winning them back.

Small Town PAC is about helping put power back in the hands of our
neighbors and building a party that takes these places seriously again.
It’s about expanding the map, supporting leaders who actually understand
these communities, and fighting for the schools, jobs, and future small
towns deserve.

* $17 million would buy you nearly **11,000 tickets to a UNC vs. Duke basketball game**(that’s more than all of Cameron stadium).

Now we’re not asking you to write a $17 million check, Peter. But it’d take 680,000 grassroots donors giving $25 for our campaign to go toe-to-toe with their dark-money spending.
